anchor.m10.simultaneous_rb_crosstalk.corrected_form: the joint decay's (1 - p)(2^n - 1)/2^n is an error per layer of n Cliffords, so it matches the layer composition (to 0.9 %), not twice the per-Clifford one: simultaneous RB is no evidence of crosstalk errors adding in amplitude; the ions' gates cost 13x more under simultaneous operation than alone (35x per layer), and the two marginals differ by a factor 3 although their compositions agree to 0.2 %, so coherent cancellation within a sequence is ion-dependent on this chain
anchor.m10.simultaneous_rb_crosstalk.equation: both ions driven by independent Clifford sequences (2000 shots, two sequences, m = 1, 128, 512). Per-qubit MARGINAL survival (Gambetta et al. 2012) 0.9995, 0.9495, 0.938 on ion 0 and 0.998, 0.96375, 0.79925 on ion 1, giving marginal p 0.999738 and 0.999227 and r_q = (1 - p_q)/2 = 1.31e-4 and 3.87e-4, mean 2.588(94)e-4 against 1.97e-5 for the ion benchmarked alone -- a factor 13 that single-ion RB cannot see. The per-qubit composition (each kind's GATE_LOCAL channel reduced to THAT ONE qubit, so the neighbour's crosstalk rotation counts) is r_channel.q0 = 2.853e-4 and r_channel.q1 = 2.858e-4, mean 2.855e-4, which the measured mean matches to 9 %. The same run's JOINT survival P(00) = 0.9975, 0.91425, 0.75225 fits p = 0.999078(86), so (1 - p)(2^n - 1)/2^n = 6.91(7)e-4 per LAYER of two Cliffords -- 35x the isolated r -- against the layer composition r_channel_joint_layer = 6.853e-4, which it matches to 0.9 %

anchor.m3.itano_three_beam_optimum.corrected_form: one beam along x leaves <n_y> growing linearly: an unaddressed axis has heating = cooling = 2D exactly, so W_m = 0, no steady state exists (CoolingError) and <n>(t) = n_0 + 2D t; UncooledModeError is the same statement as a refusal
anchor.m3.itano_three_beam_optimum.equation: axis i takes friction from its own beam only (proportional to gamma_si) and the emission recoil from all three (f_si gamma_tot), so E_i is proportional to 1 + f_si gamma_tot/gamma_si and minimizing sum_i E_i at fixed sum_i gamma_si gives gamma_si proportional to sqrt(f_si); at that optimum E_i = (hbar Gamma/4)(1 + sqrt(f_si) sum_j sqrt(f_sj)). For an isotropic pattern (f_si = 1/3, the Cartesian sum rule of Section 4.2.8) the shares are 1/3 each and E_i = hbar Gamma/2 per mode, whose kinetic half is EXACTLY Itano's hbar Gamma/4 per mode, the same number as the single-beam (1 + alpha)/4 form at alpha = 1. For the sigma pattern along z (f = 3/10, 3/10, 2/5) the shares are (0.3169873, 0.3169873, 0.3660254) and the optimum total is 5.9856 hbar Gamma/4 against the uniform split's 6
anchor.m3.itano_three_beam_optimum.source: Itano and Wineland, Phys. Rev. A 25, 35 (1982) Eqs. 20-26; qutip_trap.prep.closed_forms
anchor.m3.itano_three_beam_optimum.symbol: gamma_si/gamma_tot = sqrt(f_si)/sum_j sqrt(f_sj); hbar Gamma/4 per mode

anchor.m3a.optical_pumping.corrected_form: the photon count needs the coherent oscillations of the photon rate resolved (5 ns sampling): a 100 ns grid aliases them to 2.83 photons
anchor.m3a.optical_pumping.equation: 171Yb+ pumped on F = 1 -> F' = 1 at s_o = 0.5, 5 G, magic-angle polarization, by the exact exponential of the 64-dimensional Liouvillian: 99 percent in |0,0> at 2.6 us, 3.00 photons scattered on average (1/3 branching into |0> per excitation), residual F = 1 population 2e-6 from the 12.6 GHz off-resonant F = 0 -> F' = 1 excitation; at s_o = 0.02 the level-C curve agrees with the weak-drive rate equations built from the Lorentzian excitation rates and the channel branchings to 0.01

anchor.m3a.phonon_rate_equation.equation: mesolve on {sqrt(eta^2 A_+) a^dag, sqrt(eta^2 A_-) a} with A_+ = 3e4, A_- = 4e5 s^-1, eta = 0.1, n_0 = 5, 40 Fock levels reproduces the closed form to 3.73e-13 in <n> over 3 ms; the birth-death generator has zero column sums and the geometric stationary distribution (A_+/A_-)^n; A_- <= A_+ raises CoolingError rather than returning a negative occupation

anchor.m3a.yb171_leakage_prefactors.corrected_form: the angular algebra settles the Noek-Crain factor 2 in Noek's favour; R_d depends on the field through the bright-manifold redistribution (346.9 Hz at 1 G, near Crain's measured 341(13) Hz where the fluorescence is only 0.24 of its optimum), so the measured triple constrains the apparatus, not the prefactor
anchor.m3a.yb171_leakage_prefactors.equation: from the slowest Liouvillian eigenvalue and the stationary weights: at s_o = 0.1, B = 1 G, R_d = 9.9734 Hz (Noek's (2/3)(1/3) form with s = s_o/3: 9.9208; Crain's 1/3: 14.881), R_b = 0.60939 Hz (Noek's (2/3) form 0.60634), R_b/R_d = 0.0611 (3/49 = 0.06122); at Crain's s_o = 2.45 and the fluorescence-optimal 4.7 G, R_d = 248.9 Hz (Noek 243.1, Crain 364.6) and R_b = 14.93 Hz (14.86), the slow mode separated from the fast ones by 3e3 to 3e4
anchor.m3a.yb171_leakage_prefactors.symbol: R_d = (2/27)(Gamma/2) s_o (Gamma/2 Delta_HFP)^2, R_b = (2/9)(Gamma/2) s_o (Gamma/(2(Delta_HFP + Delta_HFS)))^2

anchor.m3a.yb171_repump_level_gap.corrected_form: the D manifold and the repump beams of Section 8.1 need that constant cited; the two-tone 935 nm repump (3.07 GHz sideband) is otherwise the Floquet-fallback case the builder handles
anchor.m3a.yb171_repump_level_gap.equation: Olmschenk 2007 prints no lifetime or branching for the 935 nm upper level (its Sec. II says the ion 'quickly returns' to S1/2 and cites Bell et al., PRA 44, R20 (1991)), so the D3/2 -> 3D[3/2]1/2 -> S1/2 repump cycle cannot be closed from cited constants; the 171Yb+ detection model folds the 0.501 percent D3/2 branch back into the S line (leak = renormalize, a 0.5 percent effect on the saturation denominator) or routes it to a sink state that fills at Gamma_D P_e (leak = sink, trace preserved, about 200 photons before the ion is dark without a repump)

anchor.m4.baldwin_echo.corrected_form: the printed H fixes only |Phi|: the printed diag(1, i, i, 1) belongs to the other detuning side
anchor.m4.baldwin_echo.equation: the printed H = eta Omega sum_j (-1)^j (1 + sigma_z^j)(a e^{i delta t} + h.c.) integrated through R_x(pi) U R_-x(pi) U at 8 pi (eta Omega/delta)^2 = pi/4 gives diag(1, -i, -i, 1) up to a global phase for tones above the mode (the conjugate of the printed diag(1, i, i, 1), whose sign the detuning side sets); off-diagonal elements vanish; Phi_loop = 2 pi (eta Omega/delta)^2 on S^2 per loop

anchor.m4.fm_and_fourier_robustness.corrected_form: five and seven vertices leave the robust system underdetermined for two modes (four closure plus four robustness residuals)
anchor.m4.fm_and_fourier_robustness.equation: two-mode fixture: Leung's nine-vertex FM schedule closes both modes and the robust cost nulls the time-averaged trajectory, so a common 500 Hz drift costs 4e-6 against 9e-4 for the unconstrained schedule; Blumel's first-order stabilized sixteen-function Fourier pulse nulls d alpha/d omega_m and is far less sensitive to a 1 kHz shift than the unstabilized one

anchor.m4.kirchmair_ca40.corrected_form: the 25 us point is eps/2pi = 40 kHz (tau = K/eps); F = 0.993(1) and 0.971(2) are not reproduced from eta and nu, whose intrinsic residual-displacement and Debye-Waller terms at nbar = 0 are below 1e-5: the technical terms of Section 4.4.7 (2e-3 from carrier excitation by laser frequency noise, heating Gamma_h t_g/2, delta Omega/Omega = 1.4e-2 costing 4.8e-4) dominate and fit inside 1 - F = 7e-3 at 50 us
anchor.m4.kirchmair_ca40.equation: at nu/2pi = 1.232 MHz and eta = 0.044 the closure algebra fixes the apparatus: t_g = 50 us is eps/2pi = 20 kHz at K = 1 and needs Omega/2pi = 227.3 kHz, t_g = 25 us is eps/2pi = 40 kHz and needs 454.5 kHz, i.e. Omega/nu = 0.369. The one closed-form prediction among the row's numbers is the nbar = 20(2) parity contrast, |sum_n P_n e^{-i 4 chi_0 eta^2 n}| = 0.9923 against the paper's 0.964, agreeing to 2.9%

anchor.m4.residual_displacement_conversi.corrected_form: Zhu's printed sum beta (|alpha_j|^2 + |alpha_n|^2)/4 is one quarter of the direct integration for the |dd> input with Choi's alpha, consistent only if Zhu's alpha is twice Choi's (his Eq. 8 is inconsistent with his Eq. 7 by that factor); it is not a distinct fidelity measure
anchor.m4.residual_displacement_conversi.equation: an open loop (1.3 loops) with the first-order force: the final mode energy equals sum_j |alpha_j|^2, 1 - F_ent = eps_ent to first order, the average gate infidelity is (4/5) eps_ent, and the |dd> state infidelity equals eps_ent

anchor.m4.solvers_verified_by_exact_inte.corrected_form: the PM family's leakage is an order of magnitude above the others' because its motion phase is its modulation parameter and Roos's spin-axis tilt cannot be tuned away (conv.pm_solver)
anchor.m4.solvers_verified_by_exact_inte.equation: every solution is verified by exact integration of the full Hamiltonian through the PulseEngine; on the two-ion fixture: FM (dims [2,2,11,10]) exact chi/surrogate = 0.9847 with leakage 4.7e-4, stabilized Fourier AM (dims [2,2,10,10]) 0.9831 with leakage 4.7e-7, PM (dims [2,2,11,12]) 0.9528 with leakage 1.8e-2; boundary populations below 1e-15 throughout

anchor.m5.crain_corrections_and_operatin.corrected_form: Crain's 11 us is the AVERAGE detection time of the stop-on-first-photon protocol (a bright ion stops at its first photon after 2 us), not the record window; the closed-form optimum window is 20 to 25 us
anchor.m5.crain_corrections_and_operatin.equation: Eq. 1 sums to 1 only with the no-jump branch (0.0068 without at 20 us); Eq. 3 at 11 us: 6.26e-3 corrected against 7.18e-4 printed; the zero-threshold average error has its minimum 5.84e-4 at 21.5 us (5.39e-4 without background) against the measured 6.9e-4 at 11 us average detection time

anchor.m5.crosstalk_depumping.corrected_form: the pumping is frozen at the neighbours' start classes, the first-order form the factored confusion tensor uses, because one ion's chain is sampled before its neighbours' paths are known; the polarization share of the leaked light that reaches the pumping channel is a device parameter defaulting to the bound of 1
anchor.m5.crosstalk_depumping.equation: the leaked resonant light of a bright neighbour at spacing x has s_nb = 3 lambda^2/(8 pi^2 x^2) (Acton's bound with the corrected I_sat = pi h c Gamma/(3 lambda^3)), and R_d, R_b are linear in intensity with no saturation denominator (Section 8.1), so one bright neighbour adds (R_d, R_b) x s_nb/s_beam to the ion's chain, several neighbours adding linearly; at 369.5 nm and 14 um s_nb = 2.65e-5, so at Crain's s_o = 2.45 one neighbour adds 3.7 mHz to R_d = 341 Hz and 0.18 mHz to R_b = 16.4 Hz. R_o is untouched: Wineland's mechanism degrades DISCRIMINATION, never eta_d
anchor.m5.crosstalk_depumping.symbol: Delta R_d, Delta R_b per bright neighbour

anchor.m5.myerson_optimum_and_recursion.corrected_form: the measured optimum sits at a higher threshold and a longer window than the ideal-Poisson one because the PMT dark counts are non-Poissonian (the paper attributes about 20 % of eps_D to cosmic rays), which the model does not carry
anchor.m5.myerson_optimum_and_recursion.equation: recursion equals brute force to 1e-14 in log; with ideal Poisson statistics the exact chain's optimum is eps = 1.24e-4 at n_c = 3.5, t_b = 320 us and 1.37e-4 at the paper's (5.5, 420 us) against the measured 1.8(1)e-4; time-resolved ML Monte Carlo eps_D ~ 1.0e-4 to 1.5e-4 with eps_B <= 5e-5 (paper 1.5(2)e-4, asymptote 0.87e-4); adaptive 60/177 us average (paper 72/219 us)

anchor.m5.yb171_rate_object.corrected_form: R_o = 0.0880 Gamma is at Noek's s = 0.815, i.e. s_o = 2.45 (the two saturation parameters of Section 8.8 are not aliases); at s_o = 0.815 the form gives 0.0383 Gamma
anchor.m5.yb171_rate_object.equation: the Bloch solve through rates_from_bloch: R_o/closed = 0.9948 (s_o = 0.1, 1 G) and 0.9969 (2.45, 4.7 G) with the ceiling 1/4 asserted; R_d and R_b within 0.5 to 2.4 % of Noek's prefactors; R_b/R_d = 0.0611 and 0.0600 against 3/49 = 0.0612 and the measured 0.048 (30 % band)

anchor.m6.bell_state.corrected_form: the row asks for agreement with the ideal statevector within the readout errors: |P00 - 0.5| = 1.5e-3 at a 7.9e-3 error bar; the exact spot check of the gate leaves 1.3e-4 while the (Omega/nu)^2 carrier scale bounds it at 6.6e-3
anchor.m6.bell_state.equation: 4000-shot histogram 00: 0.5015, 11: 0.4965, 01: 0.0013, 10: 0.0008 against the ideal 0.5/0.5 (error bar on P00 0.0079); register 1 - F = 2.336e-3 against the compiled circuit's state, inside the intrinsic budget 3.0e-2 (carrier scale 6.6e-3, Bessel saturation 2.1e-2, five gpi2 crosstalk terms of 3.0e-4, Debye-Waller 4.1e-6); detection threshold 0.5 at a 20 us window with (eps_B, eps_D) = (6.05e-4, 4.18e-4) from the record model, SPAM per qubit (6.1e-4, 3.5e-4) at zero crosstalk, preparation error 2.48e-6; Doppler nbar 3.5 to 11.6 falls to 0.0185/0.0154 on the gate modes after 40 sideband pulses; six branches carry all but 3.4e-5; parity contrast 0.99712, Bell bound (P00 + P11 + C)/2 = 0.99768
anchor.m6.bell_state.source: the two-ion 171Yb+ example device, qutip_trap.device.presets (global 355 nm pair at 100.93 kHz, 2.5 um addressing pairs with eps = 0.0220, oblique 369.5 nm cooling and detection beam, Crain SNSPD)
anchor.m6.bell_state.symbol: two-ion Bell circuit through run() (Section 9.6 row 1)

anchor.m6.section_11_1_native_identity.corrected_form: the off-resonant carrier term is (Omega_tone/(2 nu))^2 (the measured 4.66e-05 is about 2 x 1.14e-04/4 for the two ions), not (Omega/nu)^2 = 4.49e-04; run.job.intrinsic_budget's carrier_scale computes (2 pi peak/nu_min)^2 = 5.144e-04 here and so overstates that term by 4.5 in every reported budget total
anchor.m6.section_11_1_native_identity.equation: the exact play (no Lamb-Dicke expansion, no RWA), calibrated to chi = pi/4 by the exact spot check at Omega_tone/2pi = 64.148 kHz, reproduces the native matrix from |00>|0> with 1 - F = 4.659e-05, inside the off-resonant carrier excitation (Omega_tone/(2 nu))^2 = 1.1430e-04 (1.1228e-04 at the closed-form amplitude, before the 0.9 % spot-check correction); with lamb_dicke_order = 1 and rwa = True in the interaction frame 1 - F = 2.32e-10, inside 1e-6; the closed-form closure eta Omega/eps lands at 0.499583, not 1/2 (a 8.3e-4 correction from the |alpha|^2 term of the Section 4.4.3 kernel); the Bessel force saturation at the top of the carried range (n = 11, eta = 0.0786) is 3.055e-02
anchor.m6.section_11_1_native_identity.source: qutip_trap.run.job (intrinsic_budget) on the two-ion 171Yb+ fixture: x-COM 3.0000 MHz, eta = 0.078577 on both ions, tones inside the sideband at eps/2pi = 10 kHz, one 100 us loop, d_m = 12, joint dimension 48, no noise, no light shift
anchor.m6.section_11_1_native_identity.symbol: the Section 11.1 pulse against MS(0, 0, pi/2)

anchor.m7.hughes_two_term.corrected_form: lambda^2_{S_alpha} and lambda^2_{S_alpha^2} are the variances of the two spin operators over the input state, not the bare moments: the second is <S^4> - <S^2>^2 = 2N(N - 1), and reading it as <S^4> = 3N^2 - 2N overshoots by 2 at N = 2 and 1.75 at N = 3
anchor.m7.hughes_two_term.equation: alpha_t = int_0^{t_g} eps(t) gamma(t) dt and delta_theta = 2 int_0^{t_g} eps(t)|gamma(t)|^2 dt with H_e = hbar eps(t) a^dag a (Eq. 29) and U_g = exp{(gamma a^dag - gamma* a) S_alpha} exp{-i (theta/2) S_alpha^2} (Eq. 27); for a constant fractional offset on a symmetric K-loop gate |alpha_t| = (pi sqrt K/2)(eps/delta) and delta_theta = (pi/2)(eps/delta), the second K-independent; exact two- and three-ion propagation of the force model gives an exact-to-closed-form ratio extrapolating to 1.0000 with a linear-in-eps remainder (0.990568, 0.995311, 0.997671, 0.998873 at eps/delta = 4e-3, 2e-3, 1e-3, 5e-4 for N = 2, K = 1, nbar = 0 -> 1.000076), at every (N, K, nbar) in {(2,1,0), (2,1,1), (2,2,0), (3,1,0), (3,1,2), (2,3,0)}
anchor.m7.hughes_two_term.source: Hughes et al., arXiv:2510.17286 (2025), Appendix B Eq. 33

anchor.m7.intensity_noise_factor_two.corrected_form: superseded by anchor.m7.intensity_noise_n_ions, which carries the derivation and the measurements
anchor.m7.intensity_noise_factor_two.equation: the measured A/(Gamma_I t_g eta^2/2) is N (1.00, 2.00, 3.01, 2.00, 2.00, 3.00 at (N, K) = (1,1), (2,1), (3,1), (2,2), (2,3), (3,2)), not a factor 2: A is exact at N = 1 with the carrier-contrast Gamma_I
anchor.m7.intensity_noise_factor_two.symbol: the factor N of the intensity-noise infidelity

anchor.m7.intensity_noise_n_ions.corrected_form: the Gamma_I convention is settled: A = Gamma_I t_g eta^2/2 is exact at N = 1 with Gamma_I the carrier-contrast rate k Omega^2, and an N-ion drive multiplies both terms by N (Var(sum s_i) = N, Hughes's lambda^2_{S_alpha}); only a global intensity-noise operator gives B/A = 3(N-1)/(4K), while N independent per-beam operators leave A(N) unchanged and halve the ratio to 3(N-1)/(8K), so the B term describes one laser shared by the register
anchor.m7.intensity_noise_n_ions.equation: in the sigma_alpha eigenbasis block s closes with a residual displacement s x delta_alpha, <|delta_alpha|^2> = f^2 (2 Gamma_I/Omega^2) t_g with f = eta Omega/2; the pair (s, s') decoheres by exp(-|s - s'|^2 <|delta_alpha|^2>(2 nbar + 1)/2), so 1 - F = Var(sum_i s_i)(2 nbar + 1)(eta^2/2) Gamma_I t_g and Var = N for |0...0>. Measured A/(Gamma_I t_g eta^2/2) = 1.00002, 2.00035, 3.00622, 2.00003, 1.99998, 3.00038 at (N, K) = (1,1), (2,1), (3,1), (2,2), (2,3), (3,2), and B/[Gamma_I t_g eta^2 3(N - 1)/(8K)] = 1.99939, 2.99441, 1.99989, 2.00005, 2.99922: a factor N in both terms; B/A = 3(N-1)/(4K) exactly (0.74964, 1.49411, 0.37497, 0.25001, 0.74971)
anchor.m7.intensity_noise_n_ions.source: Bermudez 2017, re-derived (force model, d = 40, k = 2e-6, eta = 0.1, mesolve atol 1e-12); qutip_trap.validation.noise_closed_forms
anchor.m7.intensity_noise_n_ions.symbol: A = N Gamma_I t_g eta^2/2, B = A x 3(N - 1)/(4K)

anchor.m8.compensation_phase_reference.corrected_form: without the phase reference the Bell circuit through run() reads 4.196e-3 (2.333e-3 with it) and the three-ion GHZ circuit 5.25e-2
anchor.m8.compensation_phase_reference.equation: with the tone phase referenced to t = 0: 2.9e-5, 1.45e-2, 5.7e-2 for delta_s = -38.4 Hz, i.e. sin^2(pi delta_s t_start) / 2 = (2 pi delta_s t_start)^2/4 for small angles (0.24 and 0.48 rad); with compensation_phase_rad: 2.9e-5 at every start. A five-segment MS gate 500 us into a schedule with the per-gate beat reset the fixture's hardware uses: 1.3e-4 as at t = 0 (4.8e-4 with the beat note left running, Roos's tilt, Section 7.10)
anchor.m8.compensation_phase_reference.source: qutip_trap.control.schedule on the two-ion 171Yb+ circuit fixture, JOINT_EXACT
anchor.m8.compensation_phase_reference.symbol: 1 - F of a compensated GPi2 at t_start = 0, 1 ms, 2 ms

anchor.m8.full_calibration_two_ion.corrected_form: a 4-sigma bound per entry and a fidelity bound of budget + 3 x cal + 2e-3 with no lower bound would pass a substantially worse calibration and equally one whose errors had disappeared (a table played as the physics)
anchor.m8.full_calibration_two_ion.equation: every entry the experiments fit (field, qubit frequencies, mode frequencies, occupations, Rabi frequencies, light shifts, crosstalk ratios and phases, the entangling waveform's closure and phase alignment, detection) agrees with the device's derived truth within two of its reported standard errors (the realized deviations are all at or below 1.02 sigma); a Bell circuit run from the fitted table reaches a register infidelity inside the intrinsic budget plus the calibration's own contribution (the per-pulse over-rotation (sigma_Omega/Omega x pi/2)^2 and the residual frame offset (2 pi sigma_f t_gate)^2, with no slack factor) and strictly above the surrogate-table run's
anchor.m8.full_calibration_two_ion.source: qutip_trap.calibration.experiments on the two-ion 171Yb+ fixture (reduced scans: 400 shots per point)

anchor.m9a.gate_local_bell.corrected_form: the tracked occupation is compared with the joint run's branch-weighted reduced state, not with its first (vacuum) branch
anchor.m9a.gate_local_bell.equation: register populations (00, 01, 10, 11) JOINT_EXACT (0.508139, 0.000489, 0.001267, 0.490104) against GATE_LOCAL (0.508170, 0.000484, 0.001241, 0.490105), max difference 3.0e-5 against the reported bound 2.5e-4 (residual displacement 9.3e-5, the carrier steps' frozen-mode excitation 1.6e-4); register 1 - F 2.333e-3 against 2.287e-3; the MS step on the 572-dimensional gate-local space [2, 2, 11, 13]: average gate infidelity 1.14e-4, depolarizing rate 1.42e-4, twirl p_II 0.99986, residual |alpha| per spin eigenstate 2.7e-3 (rocking) and 9.1e-3 (COM), purity deficit of the reduced motional state 4.0e-2 and 3.4e-2, tracked nbar 0.02027 and 0.01726 against the joint run's branch-weighted reduced state; 344 engine runs (16 inputs x 3 branches per gate step)
anchor.m9a.gate_local_bell.symbol: GATE_LOCAL against JOINT_EXACT, two-ion Bell circuit

anchor.m9a.tomography_projection.corrected_form: a positive-semidefinite projection alone leaves Tr_out(Choi) != 1, a map that changes the register's normalization on every application; the projection ends on the trace-preserving set and reports the remaining distance to the cone
anchor.m9a.tomography_projection.equation: the Choi matrix of MS(0.3, -0.7, pi/2) from its sixteen product inputs equals choi_from_unitary to 5e-16 with one Kraus operator; a depolarizing channel (eps = 0.05) reconstructed from outputs carrying 3e-4 of noise violates trace preservation at the noise level and the alternating projection returns ||Tr_out(Choi) - 1|| and the distance to the cone both below 1e-10, the map within 5e-3 of the truth, the twirl p_II = 0.95 and the depolarizing rate equal to the entanglement infidelity (Chen 2023's normalization)

anchor.m9b.cost_model_constants.corrected_form: '24 against 512 amplitudes' counts multiply-adds; the measured gain is smaller and set by the fixed cost of each NumPy call (about 3 us per factor), so the auto rule is a measured crossover, and the assembled operator stays the right choice below dimension 440
anchor.m9b.cost_model_constants.equation: one right-hand side through QobjEvo.matmul (dispatch included), least-squares fit over eleven spaces from dimension 48 to 8192: a factorized term costs about 2.9 us per factor step plus 0.58 ns per complex multiply-add on the D/d_ion amplitudes of the source level, an assembled CSR term 0.57 ns per non-zero (2^{N-1} prod_m d_m^2 for two-level ions); the kernel carries 2.0 us + 2.5 us per step + 0.6 ns per multiply-add against 0.5 us + 0.57 ns per non-zero, which reproduces the measured choice on every space: assembled at dimensions 48 (0.7 against 4.7 us) and 256 (5.2 against 8.2), factorized from the 440-dimensional Bell space (14.3 against 9.8) upward, 299 against 24 us at 2048 and 1196 against 69 us at 8192 (four ions, three modes at d_m = 8)

anchor.m9b.factorized_kernel_exactness.corrected_form: an ENR group's sum-generator exponential is not a product of per-mode factors (Section 5.1.1), so a drive coupling to an ENR mode is assembled whatever the option says; a sum of two factorized operators has no factorized form and converts to Dense (the reason QobjEvo.compress must never merge the drive terms: every term carries its own coefficient object), and every mesolve segment builds the assembled CSR operator because the Liouvillian is formed from the matrix (Section 5.3)
anchor.m9b.factorized_kernel_exactness.equation: the drive operator held as its tensor factors (sigma_+ on the ion's factor, the oracle-checked per-mode exponentials D_m(i eta_m) on the resolved modes) and applied axis by axis (the ion factor a slice of the source level into the target level, every mode factor one batched matrix product) is the assembled operator to round-off: |F psi - A psi| = 2.4e-16 on the Bell space [2, 2, 10, 11] and 5.0e-16 at dimension 2048, max|F - A| = 0 element by element, the adjoint, the factor-wise F^dag F (9e-15) and the trace exact; registered as a QuTiP data-layer type so that QobjEvo, sesolve, mcsolve and the dop853/vern9 ladder run unchanged on it; the 20 us single-loop pulse through the engine with the kernel forced each way gives |psi_assembled - psi_factorized| = 2.2e-13 with identical populations (0.491426, 0.0252973, 0.0252973, 0.4579794)

anchor.raman.wineland_2_3.corrected_form: the complex phase is recorded and may be set to zero once per ion (Section 4.3.4)
anchor.raman.wineland_2_3.equation: the two-photon coupling Omega e^{i phi} with the effective wavevector Delta k = k_1 - k_2 substituted for k (|Delta k| = 2 k sin(theta/2) at crossing angle theta; 2k counter-propagating; 0 co-propagating, where every eta vanishes)

anchor.species.ba_g_factors.corrected_form: NIST ASD's Lande column for Ba II returns 0.79, 1.12 and 1.32 and nothing for 6s 2S1/2: its 1.12 for D5/2 is ASD's own error (6.7 % from the measured 1.20036739(24), Hoffman et al. 2013's 1.200372(4)(7) and the LS Lande 1.2005); both ASD readings stay as contested cross-checks nothing consumes, and the 6p levels take the LS Lande 0.665894 and 1.334106 (background)
anchor.species.ba_g_factors.equation: the three Ba+ S and D g factors are measured: g_J(6s 2S1/2) = 2.00249192(3) (Marx et al. 1998, Penning trap on 138Ba+ and 135Ba+; read in Arnold et al. 2020, hence extracted), stored in both isotope tables since g_J is isotope-independent to 3e-8; g_J(5d 2D3/2) = 0.7993278(3) (Knoell et al. 1996, extracted); g_J(5d 2D5/2) = 1.20036739(24) (Arnold et al. 2020, the measured ratio 0.59943681(12) times g_S, reproduced to 2.1e-9); 137Ba+'s clock qubit then reproduces taylor_c2 = (g_J - g_I)^2 mu_B^2/(2 h^2 nu_0) = 488.81912 Hz/G^2 at nu_0 = 8 037 741 667.69 Hz to 1e-9, which nothing published pins; the qubit pair, cycling line, repumps and shelving line of ba137.species() are this package's choice
anchor.species.ba_g_factors.source: Marx, Tommaseo, Werth, Eur. Phys. J. D 4, 279 (1998); Knoell et al., Phys. Rev. A 54, 1199 (1996); Arnold et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 124, 193001 (2020), arXiv:1906.09150; NIST ASD ver. 5.12 Ba II Lande column; qutip_trap.species.ba137; qutip_trap.species.ba133

anchor.trap.berkeland_excess_micromotion.corrected_form: the carrier sign inverts past the first zero at beta = 2.4048; Berkeland's Eq. 21 prints a stray factor Omega

anchor.trap.depth_optima.corrected_form: the c = b/2 branch extrapolates a formula House derived for c = b only: the House formula applied to unequal rails is 8 to 40% off the numerical saddle at Nizamani's design point
anchor.trap.depth_optima.equation: depth maximal at b/a = 1.1914879 = cbrt(54 - 6 sqrt 33)/6 + cbrt(54 + 6 sqrt 33)/6 for fixed a; at fixed ion height b/a = 3.676 with kappa = 0.022542 = (5 sqrt 5 - 11)/8 for c = b, and 4.902 with 0.020038 = 8/9 of it for c = b/2; Nizamani's kappa equals House's Eq. 29 for c = b

anchor.trap.heating_dynamics.corrected_form: not Gamma_h (2 N_bar + 1)(n0 + m0); the +1 is the absorption channel on the lower level
anchor.trap.heating_dynamics.equation: mesolve with sqrt(Gamma_h) a and sqrt(Gamma_h) a^dag gives n_bar(t) = Gamma_h t to 2e-3; the coherence of (|n0> + |m0>)/sqrt 2 decays at Gamma_h (n0 + m0 + 1): 2.01, 4.03, 10.09 Gamma_h over a short window for (0, 1), (1, 2), (3, 6)

anchor.trap.james_spectrum.corrected_form: James Table 1 positions are reproduced through these eigenvalue anchors and the closed forms

anchor.trap.kielpinski_three_ion.corrected_form: mode order is not monotonic in mu, so modes are identified by eigenvector structure, not by index
anchor.trap.kielpinski_three_ion.equation: 0.7811, 1.7321, 1.8881 at mu = 24/9 and 1.1093, 1.7321, 3.5454 at 9/24 from both the closed forms and the mass-weighted Hessian (1e-6); zeta_2 = sqrt 3 with zero impurity amplitude for all mu; zeta_3(17/3) = sqrt 3; zeta_3(7.3) = 1.7034 < zeta_2; gaps 1.560 and 6.228 MHz at f_z = 10 MHz

anchor.trap.stability_edge.corrected_form: the printed continued fractions of RMP 2003 Eqs. 10-11 carry an index error and are not used
anchor.trap.stability_edge.equation: the monodromy trace reaches -2 at q = 0.9080 for a = 0 (Mathieu tables: 0.908); beta^2 - (a + q^2/2) = O(q^4)

anchor.trap.zigzag_threshold.corrected_form: the fit 0.73 N^0.86 is 13 to 32% off (negative control); sqrt(12/5) is the ratio, not alpha_crit
anchor.trap.zigzag_threshold.equation: alpha_crit = 2/(mu_N - 1) = 1, 5/12 at N = 2, 3; (omega_r/omega_z)_crit = 1.0000, 1.5492, 2.4975, 4.5957, 6.5396, 7.2931, 11.9930 for N = 2, 3, 5, 10, 15, 17, 30; solve_crystal raises ZigzagError below it

conv.appendix_e_signatures.corrected_form: a Drive stores beam indices, not wavevectors, so its Delta k needs the device's beams
conv.appendix_e_signatures.equation: Drive.delta_k is a method taking the device's beams (a Drive stores beam indices); MetastableChannels.bbr_rate_hz takes the Species that owns the line; DecouplingSequence.rounded_to_clock returns (sequence, residual moments); CombSpec.pair_order_max = None derives the Stark-sum depth from the envelope

conv.be9_g_j_provenance.corrected_form: the circulating 2.0022621287(24) is a calculation (Dickopf et al. 2024, printed negative in their sign convention), stored as be9.S12.g_J_theory (background) and not a replacement: the two agree to 2.61e-7 (0.84 sigma), and swapping them moves the 119.446 G clock point by 1.56e-5 G and 0.0093 Hz, against 0.135 G and 81 Hz for g_J = 2.000; Dickopf et al. is Nature 632, 757-761 (2024), not 673
conv.be9_g_j_provenance.equation: g_J = 2.00226239(31) is measured: Wineland, Bollinger and Itano 1983 compared the cyclotron frequency with a hyperfine-Zeeman transition frequency at the same field (their printed 2.00226206(42)), and Shiga et al. 2011 Sec. I re-reduce it with CODATA 2006's proton-electron mass ratio (their abstract gives only the ratio g_I'/g_J)
conv.be9_g_j_provenance.source: Shiga, Itano, Bollinger, Phys. Rev. A 84, 012510 (2011), arXiv:1106.5760, Sec. I; Wineland, Bollinger, Itano, Phys. Rev. Lett. 50, 628 (1983); Mohr, Taylor, Newell, Rev. Mod. Phys. 80, 633 (2008); Dickopf et al., Nature 632, 757 (2024); qutip_trap.species.be9

conv.be9_linewidth.corrected_form: the spread is far outside every stated accuracy: the ASD value implies tau = 8.86 ns and f = 0.498 (the textbook ~0.5 for a Li-like ion) while 19.4 and 19.6 MHz need f = 0.543, and no primary derivation of the trapped-ion '19.4 MHz / 8.2 ns' is known
conv.be9_linewidth.equation: four readings spanning 9 %: 17.97 MHz (NIST ASD A_ki 1.1292e8 and 1.1285e8 s^-1, accuracy grade AAA <= 0.3 %, theory), 19.4 MHz (Monroe et al. 1995), 19.6 MHz (Ozeri Table I) and 19.64 MHz (Andersen, Jessen, Soerensen 1969, beam-foil); the record uses Monroe's 19.4 MHz, which the 9Be+ anchors assume (P_SE = 8.706e-4)
conv.be9_linewidth.source: NIST ASD (Yan, Tambasco, Drake 1998); Monroe et al. 1995; Ozeri 2007 Table I; Andersen et al. 1969; qutip_trap.species.be9

conv.be9_p32_hyperfine.corrected_form: two unresolved tensions: the theory A is 1.7x larger than Bollinger 1985's bound |A(2P3/2)| < 0.6 MHz, and the theory B is negative while Q(9Be) = +0.0529(4) b is positive (sign(B) = sign(Q) for a single p3/2 electron); neither affects any anchor (a 1 MHz splitting against THz detunings), and the values are never read as measured; the circulating -1.03(3) / -2.30(9) MHz pair has invented uncertainties
conv.be9_p32_hyperfine.equation: the record uses the THEORY values A = -1.026(3) MHz and B = -2.29940(3) MHz, tagged background; no measurement of either exists
conv.be9_p32_hyperfine.source: Puchalski and Pachucki, Phys. Rev. A 79, 032510 (2009); Bollinger et al., Phys. Rev. A 31, 2711 (1985); qutip_trap.species.be9

conv.beam_phase_spectrum.corrected_form: per-beam phase trajectories make route (d) of Section 6.1 reachable for the phase-sensitive Raman geometries of Section 6.3; Kirchmair's 2e-3 per gate from incoherent carrier excitation and the Rabi-drift anchors (Kirchmair 1.4e-2, Harty 5e-4) are consistency anchors in qutip_trap.validation.noise_closed_forms
conv.beam_phase_spectrum.equation: each beam gets its own realization of the same declared spectrum, so a Raman pair's beat note sees phi_2(t) - phi_1(t) with twice one beam's variance (measured 2.00 x sigma^2 over 120 seeds) and a co-propagating pair (one shared path, declared as one beam) sees none; the builder reads the sampled Delta phi(t) (phi_2 - phi_1 for a Raman or light-shift pair, -phi_1 for a single beam) and multiplies the beat note by e^{-i Delta phi(t)}, so constant trajectories reproduce the quasi-static build to 1e-12 and a common-mode path drift cancels; the Baldwin form's (4 g^2/Delta^2) enters squared, so halving the two-photon-to-detuning ratio drops eps by exactly 4
conv.beam_phase_spectrum.symbol: NoiseModel.beam_phase_noise -> phi_j(t) per beam; eps = [int S_phi F] (4 g^2/Delta^2)^2

conv.beat_phase_at_gate_start.corrected_form: the builder's per-pulse phase_mode='reset' resets at every segment of a multi-segment waveform (0.2-cycle jumps at the segment edges of an AM pulse open the loops: leakage 0.31); on the two-ion fixture the same calibrated gate has fidelity 0.99995 at zeta = 0 or pi and 0.98903 at zeta = +-pi/2, so a gate started 21.27 beat cycles into a circuit under continuous tones is not the gate that was calibrated
conv.beat_phase_at_gate_start.equation: with HardwareChain.phase_continuous = False every leg of an entangling waveform carries the phase offset 2 pi mu_leg t_g (red and blue opposite, the spin phase unchanged, the virtual-Z frame intact), so the beat note starts at zero phase at the gate start as it did in the t = 0 calibration; with phase-continuous tones the start phase zeta = 2 pi mu t_g is part of the gate and the tilt sin^2[(4 Omega-bar/mu) sin zeta] is reported in the intrinsic budget

conv.bermudez_pauli_mapping.equation: the three-variant mapping of eps onto Pauli channels that Sections 6.8 and 4.4.7 name has no formulas in this specification, so it is not implemented; qutip_trap.noise.summary provides the entanglement and average gate infidelity of a simulated channel, its Pauli twirl (itself a mapping onto a Pauli channel, p_Q from the Pauli transfer-matrix diagonal) and the depolarizing rate of conv.depolarizing_normalization; implementing the three variants needs the source
conv.bermudez_pauli_mapping.source: Bermudez et al., PRX 7, 041061 (2017), the fault-tolerance section; qutip_trap.noise.summary

conv.boundary_threshold_is_branch_scaled.corrected_form: the boundary trip and the margin check both read the branch-scaled threshold min(boundary_population_max / w, 0.5) on a Fock branch of weight w, one threshold on the mixture's population (what the pulse moves), and the initial cap, the monitor and the surrogate's spot-check space all take the run's boundary_population_max
conv.boundary_threshold_is_branch_scaled.equation: Section 5.5's one threshold: the population in the top two Fock levels above 1e-6 'of the population the pulse moves' repeats the run with the cap raised

conv.branching_deficit.corrected_form: an incomplete branching set is never renormalized to unity over the tabulated channels (that would put all of 40Ca+ P3/2's decay into the 393 nm line and lose its 5.9 % D-state leakage); Level.untabulated_branching declares the remainder (171Yb+ 3D[3/2]1/2 for the 297.143 nm channel)
conv.branching_deficit.equation: every upper level reached by at least one E1 transition must have its tabulated branchings plus its declared Level.untabulated_branching sum to 1 within 1e-9, and sum_{b q'} |c|^2 then equals the TABULATED total, never an unconditional 1

conv.ca40_branching.corrected_form: not the rounded 0.941/0.940, Ozeri's f^-1 = 17 (a 43Ca+ value) or a '6 % branch to D3/2' (6.8 % low): Ramm's value makes the 397 nm partial rate reproduce Hettrich's gamma_PS (23.0526 x 0.93565 = 21.5691 MHz against 21.57(8)), where 0.94 would give 21.6694 MHz
conv.ca40_branching.equation: Ramm et al. 2013's measured 0.93565(7)/0.06435(7) for the P1/2 split and Gerritsma et al. 2008's 0.93469/0.0587/0.00661 for the P3/2 split into S1/2/D5/2/D3/2
conv.ca40_branching.source: Ramm et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 111, 023004 (2013); Gerritsma et al., Eur. Phys. J. D 50, 13 (2008); qutip_trap.species.ca40

conv.ca40_linewidth_reading.corrected_form: the quoted 21.57 and 23.4 MHz are partial rates into S1/2 (Hettrich prints gamma_PS = 2 pi x 21.57(8) MHz beside gamma_PD = 2 pi x 1.482(8) MHz, and a total of 21.57 MHz would mean tau(P1/2) = 7.379 ns, which no measurement supports); the totals come from the measured lifetimes (6.904(26) ns, 23.0526 MHz; 6.639(42) ns, 23.9727 MHz), with Ramm's branching the partial rate 21.5691 MHz reproduces Hettrich's gamma_PS to 4e-5, and the quoted linewidths remain only as contested cross-checks
conv.ca40_linewidth_reading.equation: Hettrich's Table: <S1/2||d||P1/2> = 2.8928(43) e a0, tau(4p 2P1/2) = 6.904(26) ns, branching 0.93572(25), gamma_PS = 2 pi x 21.57(8) MHz and gamma_PD = 2 pi x 1.482(8) MHz, so the TOTAL is 23.05 MHz
conv.ca40_linewidth_reading.source: Hettrich et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 115, 143003 (2015); Meir et al., Phys. Rev. A 101, 012509 (2020); qutip_trap.species.ca40

conv.calibration_cache.equation: tables are cached per device configuration and noise seed; a table whose device_hash differs from the device it is asked for is never returned, so a changed parameter invalidates the old configuration's tables and the new one has none until calibrate runs (run(table=None) builds the surrogate)
conv.calibration_cache.symbol: key = (Device.hash(), seed, surrogate, experiments, t0, digest(kwargs))

conv.calibration_graph.corrected_form: a refused experiment's entries become uncalibrated, never schedulable seeds: with micromotion['beta[2]'] uncalibrated a seed fallback would leave the mode frequencies at the derived values, the fallback Section 7.3 forbids, and a Bell circuit would still schedule from that table
conv.calibration_graph.equation: calibrate(surrogate=False) runs the experiments in this order and never reorders; a downstream fit refuses to run while an entry group it reads is uncalibrated and its own entries (the groups PRODUCES names for it) become uncalibrated under its name, with the reason in CalibrationReport.refused; a group whose experiment was refused is not established even when it carries no entry to mark, and a group that is a seed because the caller did not ASK for its experiment stays a seed; seed entries (the derived values) are legitimate upstream inputs (the bootstrap)
conv.calibration_graph.symbol: crystal_image -> field -> micromotion -> modes -> rabi, stark, qubit frequency -> crosstalk -> entangling scans -> detection, heating

conv.collapse_op_rate_units.corrected_form: rates are never divided by 2 pi: the 2 pi rule of Section 5.6 converts angular frequencies, not rates, and a rate in Hz is a rate in s^-1 (the field is reporting-only)
conv.collapse_op_rate_units.equation: the field carries ndot in quanta/s, gamma_phi = 1/T_2, 2/tau and the intensity-noise and scattering densities, all ordinary rates in s^-1: heating_channels reports ndot itself (400.0 for a 400 quanta/s mode, both operators at n_bar_bath = None), motional dephasing 2/tau (250.0 at tau = 8 ms) and qubit dephasing 1/T_2 (0.6667 at T_2 = 1.5 s)

conv.collision_outcomes.corrected_form: the scale gives 7.4e4 quanta of a 1 MHz mode for H2 at 300 K on 171Yb+, above 'tens to thousands' (reached at a few MHz for a lighter ion or a heavier gas ratio), and the formula is implemented rather than tuned; a kick after the preparation discards the shot instead of adding its nbar, and a reorder permutes RunState.order and discards the shot without re-deriving b_{i,m}, eta_{i,m} or the pair sign, both declared in Diagnostics.approximations
conv.collision_outcomes.equation: <E_kick> = k_B T (m_gas/m_ion) x kick_scale_multiplier with the partial-pressure-weighted gas mass, drawn from an exponential (maximum entropy at fixed mean) or a Maxwell chi^2_3 of the same mean; <delta nbar> = <E_kick>/(hbar omega_m) on the mode it heats most (the softest); Section 6.7 states the scale, not its O(1) coefficient (the elastic head-on transfer fraction is 4 m_g/m_i and the momentum-kick estimate 3 m_g k_B T/(2 m_i), both of this order), so the coefficient is 1 and kick_scale_multiplier is the device's handle
conv.collision_outcomes.symbol: kick energy k_B T m_gas/m_ion; reorder from a configured permutation distribution

conv.comb_sum_depth.corrected_form: a literal depth of 1200 with a floor of 1000 is 2.6x too shallow at 80 MHz and 10 ps (nu_q = 12.642812118466 GHz), where the sum does not converge (79673.08 against the converged 79680.65 Hz); five half-widths leave 1.7e-5 at the Lee point, above the 1e-6 doubling tolerance, hence eight
conv.comb_sum_depth.equation: the sech^2 fourth-order weight has half-width 1/(pi nu_rep tau) in the tooth separation l (189.470 at 120 MHz and 14 ps, 397.887 at 80 MHz and 10 ps) and its tail beyond k half-widths is about 4 e^{-2k} of the sum, so CombSpec.pair_order_max = None derives the depth as eight half-widths: 1516 at the Lee point and 3184 at the Mizrahi one; 'sum to |k| >~ 1000' follows from the envelope, and an explicit pair_order_max is an override validated against the derived depth
conv.comb_sum_depth.source: Lee et al. 2016; Mizrahi et al. 2014; qutip_trap.light.comb

conv.compiler_frame_absorption.corrected_form: keeping rz in the compiled circuit would break the IonQ JSON export of Section 7.6 (rz is not an exported gate)
conv.compiler_frame_absorption.equation: every rz is absorbed into the phases of the later gpi, gpi2 and ms operations in time order (zz commutes); the compiled circuit carries only gpi, gpi2, ms, zz (the exported native set) and a residual per-qubit frame RZ(theta_q) that the computational-basis measurement cannot see; the whole-circuit check is RZ(frame) U_compiled = e^{i alpha} U_target

conv.compiler_single_qubit_decomposition.corrected_form: the ZYZ solve reads a = arg V10 - arg V00 and c = arg V11 - arg V10 (each modulo 2 pi); solving the half-sum and half-difference for a and c leaves a pi branch that flips RY(b) to RY(-b)
conv.compiler_single_qubit_decomposition.equation: GPi2(0) RZ(beta) GPi2(0) = RY(-beta) RX(pi) up to a phase, so (alpha, -beta, -gamma) are the ZYZ Euler angles of U X; a pure Z rotation is one virtual rz, a pi or pi/2 equatorial rotation one GPi or GPi2 plus an rz (H = RY(pi/2) Z is one GPi2 after a virtual Z(pi))

conv.computational_ordering.corrected_form: the computational Pauli Z of control/native.py (Z|0> = +|0>) is the negative of the energy sigma_z, and the two are never aliased
conv.computational_ordering.equation: qudit index 0 is the lower qubit level |0> = Species.qubit[0], index 1 the upper; sigma_+ = |1><0|; the ENERGY sigma_z of H_int = (Delta/2) sigma_z and H_Stark puts the upper level up; the native-gate matrices act on (|0>, |1>) as printed

conv.crosstalk_ratio.corrected_form: Schindler's printed 22/121 = 18 % is the amplitude ratio and 3.3 % the intensity ratio matching his stated < 3 % bound; the printed squared form would read 3025 %
conv.crosstalk_ratio.equation: a Rabi (amplitude) ratio from beam i onto ion j, never an intensity ratio; for a two-photon Raman pair with both beams sharing one Gaussian profile Omega is proportional to the intensity, so the amplitude ratio equals the single-beam intensity ratio at the neighbour (2.2 % for a 2.5 um waist at 3.45 um spacing)
conv.crosstalk_ratio.source: Fang 2022; Schindler 2013 (inverted and squared in print)

conv.curvature_naming.corrected_form: one field named 'curvature' silently mixes a factor 2; the missing 2 pi is 6.28 in both of Langer's figures
conv.curvature_naming.equation: d2nu_dB2 (Harty's 2.4 mHz/mG^2) and taylor_c2 = (1/2) d2nu/dB2 (Langer's 0.305 Hz/uT^2; 171Yb+'s 310.8 Hz/G^2) stored separately; accumulated phase 2 pi int [nu(B) - nu(B0)] dt with the bracket in Hz

conv.dc_floor_decoupling_sequences.corrected_form: the first-order estimate alone reports spuriously low infidelities for the band that dominates a real trap (CPMG-4 is 7x low)
conv.dc_floor_decoupling_sequences.equation: for a DecouplingSequence or Schedule no source supplies a c-hat, and c-hat (2m+1)!! rel^{m+1} is only the leading term of the exact Gaussian average of 1 - (1/4)|Tr U_c^dag U|^2 under a constant beta, so the average itself is reported (Gauss-Hermite), the larger of it and the filter-function estimate at every point; it reproduces the composite-pulse c-hat floors to 5e-4 relative (2e-3 for SCROFULOUS, whose O(beta^4) remainder is the library's largest); on a 300 Hz Gaussian band with 4 us pi pulses over 200 us: free induction 0.1237 against a first-order 0.1386, Hahn 2.30e-5 against 1.26e-3, CPMG-2 8.91e-6 against 9.03e-6, CPMG-4 8.93e-6 against 1.29e-6
conv.dc_floor_decoupling_sequences.symbol: infidelity_dc = <1 - F> over a Gaussian frozen beta (Gauss-Hermite), not c-hat (2m+1)!! rel^{m+1}

conv.dc_floor_detuning_normalization.corrected_form: pairing c-hat_d with <beta_d^2>/Omega^2 under-reports every detuning dc floor by 4^(m+1) (exact-to-reported 4.0000 at m = 0 for the primitive, SK1, BB1 and SCROFULOUS, converging to 16 for CORPSE at m = 1); the pinned floors (SK1 5.87365e-6 at var = 2.07e9/pi, Omega = 1.5e6) are the c-hat arithmetic and are unchanged
conv.dc_floor_detuning_normalization.equation: leading_coefficient fits c-hat against Mount's R = exp[-(i/2) theta (1 + eps_a)(sigma_phi + eps_d sigma_z)]. Matching that against Section 6.9's H_0 = beta . sigma (no 1/2 on the Pauli vector) gives eps_a = beta_a/Omega but eps_d = 2 beta_d/Omega, because beta_d is HALF the splitting fluctuation while eps_d scales the whole splitting. Measured: the exact frozen average of a primitive pi pulse is 4(beta_d/Omega)^2 and sin^2(pi beta_a/2 Omega) -> (pi^2/4)(beta_a/Omega)^2
conv.dc_floor_detuning_normalization.symbol: eps_d = 2 beta_d/Omega, so the detuning moment is 4 <beta_d^2>

conv.depolarizing_normalization.corrected_form: Trout 2018's p/3 and p/15 are the same weights under a different name for the parameter, not a different channel; Qiskit's lambda is NOT that p, and passing a published p to Qiskit as a lambda understates the rate by 4^n/(4^n - 1), 33 % on one qubit and 6.7 % on two. Kept separate from conv.rb_error_rate, whose p is a decay BASE, and from conv.gate_fidelity_measure, whose F_K is a unitary overlap: this row is a channel RATE
conv.depolarizing_normalization.equation: the depolarizing channel is written with the uniform weight eps/(4^n - 1) on each of the 4^n - 1 non-identity Paulis, in which eps is exactly the entanglement infidelity, so the rate the simulator reports is the entanglement infidelity and the average gate infidelity is d/(d + 1) eps, (2/3) eps at n = 1 and (4/5) eps at n = 2; as Kraus operators that is sqrt(1 - eps) 1 with sqrt(eps/3) X, Y, Z on one qubit or sqrt(eps/15) P over the fifteen non-identity two-qubit Paulis, and sum_K K^dag K = 1 to 1e-12 for every eps in [0, 1] (depolarizing_kraus); Qiskit's depolarizing_error takes the mixing weight of the maximally mixed state, lambda = eps 4^n/(4^n - 1), so Chen et al.'s Forte medians 2.0e-4 (single-qubit) and 46.4e-4 (two-qubit, direct RB) enter Qiskit as 2.67e-4 and 49.5e-4 (qiskit_depolarizing_lambda)
conv.depolarizing_normalization.source: Chen et al. 2023; Trout et al. 2018; Qiskit Aer depolarizing_error; qutip_trap.noise.summary
conv.depolarizing_normalization.symbol: Lambda_eps(rho) = (1 - eps) rho + eps/(4^n - 1) sum_{P != I} P rho P

conv.detection_efficiency_once.corrected_form: Crain's printed Eq. 3 carries the scattered R_o in the no-jump exponent, which makes it vanish and changes the bright error at 11 us by a factor 8.7 (6.26e-3 corrected against 7.18e-4 printed)
conv.detection_efficiency_once.equation: epsilon_sys enters once, in RecordModel.from_rates (scattered -> detected); the background rate is a separate additive Poisson rate; apparatus presets ingest a DETECTED rate by dividing epsilon_sys out once (rates_from_detected)

conv.detuning.corrected_form: Landsman's delta measured from a mode; Mount's dimensionless delta
conv.detuning.equation: delta from the carrier, red negative; mu = beat-note detuning from the carrier; delta_{i,m} = mu_i - omega_m always two-indexed

conv.detuning_symbols.corrected_form: Landsman's delta is measured from a mode; Mount's delta is dimensionless
conv.detuning_symbols.equation: delta = omega_L - omega_0 from the carrier; mu = beat-note detuning from the carrier; delta_{i,m} = mu_i - omega_m always two-indexed; delta-hat = eps_d = Delta/Omega, the dimensionless composite-pulse detuning error

conv.device_hash.corrected_form: Python's hash() is not supplied by frozen=True for ndarray, dict and Qobj fields
conv.device_hash.equation: canonical serialization: fields in declaration order, floats to 12 significant digits, ndarrays as dtype, shape and C-order bytes, dicts by sorted key, callables by qualified name plus a source digest, Qobj excluded, fields marked metadata hash=exclude (Device.roles) left out; the same device gives the same digest in every process

conv.doppler_optimizes_detuning_only.corrected_form: the optimization over (Delta, s, k_hat) that Section 4.2.1 names is restricted to Delta; the three-beam apportionment closed form is available separately (anchor.m3.itano_three_beam_optimum)
conv.doppler_optimizes_detuning_only.equation: only a common frequency offset of one beam group is optimized over the participation-weighted mean of the per-mode nbar; s and k_hat are inputs. The Doppler-limit nbar is nearly s independent, (Gamma/4 nu)(1 + alpha/cos^2 theta_L) sqrt(1 + s) to the force model's accuracy, but the rate that sets the stage duration depends on s and is not optimized; a three-beam geometry choice is Itano and Wineland's three_beam_optimum
conv.doppler_optimizes_detuning_only.symbol: optimize_detuning over Delta; s and k_hat fixed

conv.drive_coefficient_and_phase_continu.corrected_form: coefficients are QuTiP 5.3 f(t, **kwargs) callables carrying a shared evaluation counter, never strings (Section 5.2)
conv.drive_coefficient_and_phase_continu.equation: the beat-note phase is mu t in ABSOLUTE time for a phase-continuous tone (mu tau under phase_mode='reset'; the FM integral int mu dtau for a detuning schedule); envelopes, phases and detunings are callables of the time since the pulse start, a constant is a square pulse, an array is uniformly sampled over the pulse and cubic-spline interpolated; the static factors are rabi_scale x eps_ij x J_0(beta) x prod_frozen e^{-eta^2/2} L_n(eta^2)
conv.drive_coefficient_and_phase_continu.symbol: c(t) = (1/2) sum_tones Omega(tau) e^{-i(mu t - phi(tau))}

conv.drop_test_debye_waller_spread.corrected_form: a strengthening of the drop pair: a pulse that closes a mode's loop exactly leaves the pair at ~1e-33 however strongly the mode couples, but dropping the mode removes its exact Debye-Waller factor, whose mean the calibration absorbs and whose shot-to-shot spread eta^2 sqrt(nbar(nbar + 1)) it does not (1.5e-3 rad at nbar = 0.05 for the three-ion tilt mode, eta = 0.0809); the 3e-4 rad threshold matches the 1e-6 of the alpha^2 test, and the summed spread of the dropped modes is reported as SpaceSelection.dropped_dw_spread_rad
conv.drop_test_debye_waller_spread.equation: a mode is dropped when |alpha_m(tau)|^2 (2 nbar_m + 1) < 1e-6 AND |chi_m(tau)| < 1e-4 AND max_i eta_{i,m}^2 sqrt(nbar_m (nbar_m + 1)) < 3e-4 rad; otherwise, below the freeze pair, it is frozen

conv.dropped_mode_has_no_dynamics.corrected_form: the drop test is not intersected with the coupling test (which would leave 'dropped' unreachable and report a three-ion GHZ tilt mode with |alpha|^2 (2n+1) = 3.5e-33 as frozen), and a dropped mode is not a frozen one (no Debye-Waller factor, no Fock branch)
conv.dropped_mode_has_no_dynamics.equation: the class follows the contribution pair alone - dropped when |alpha_m|^2 (2 n_m + 1) < 1e-6 AND |chi_m| < 1e-4, whatever couples to the mode; the coupling test (|eta| > 1e-12 for some drive) decides only the modes NO entangling gate touches (no contribution): frozen when a carrier pulse couples to them, dropped when nothing does. A dropped mode has no tensor factor (like a frozen one) and additionally no Debye-Waller factor and no Fock branch, so it evolves freely and is not modelled at all, which is what makes SpaceSelection.dropped_contribution the loss nothing absorbs

conv.e2_ac_stark_shift.corrected_form: unvalidated (no source number to reproduce); the sums carry no i gamma/2, so a component degenerate with the driven one raises rather than returning an infinity
conv.e2_ac_stark_shift.equation: the ac Stark shift of a driven |S, m>-|D, m'> component by the nine off-resonant components inside the Zeeman span, second order in the same Omega(m, m') table: Delta(m, m') = 2 pi[(E_D(m0') - E_S(m0)) - (E_D(m') - E_S(m))] is a pure Zeeman offset, a component shifts its lower level by +|Omega|^2/(4 Delta) and its upper by -|Omega|^2/(4 Delta), and the driven component is excluded because the Rabi dynamics treats it exactly

conv.effective_sample_size.corrected_form: adding the within-sample binomial term mean[p_s(1 - p_s)/M_s]/S to var(p_s, ddof=1)/S counts it twice (error bars up to sqrt(2) too large: n_eff/shots = 0.547 at S = 8 on i.i.d. Bernoulli shots, where 1.0 is correct)
conv.effective_sample_size.equation: with S samples of M_s shots and per-sample frequencies p_s, the pooled estimate is p_hat = sum M_s p_s / sum M_s and Var(p_hat) = Var(p_s)/S, where Var(p_s) = sigma^2_between + p(1 - p)/M is the TOTAL per-sample variance; Var(p_s) is estimated by the shot-count-weighted sample variance sum_s M_s (p_s - p_hat)^2 / [(S - 1) sum_s M_s], which reduces to var(p_s, ddof=1)/S for equal M_s, and n_eff = p(1 - p)/Var(p_hat), the minimum over the bitstrings seen, capped at the shot count

conv.effective_wavevector.corrected_form: Landsman's k = k_2 - k_1; Lee's arXiv v1 Eq. 2 inverts its own beam-to-level assignment (the journal version is right)
conv.effective_wavevector.equation: beam 1 couples to the upper level; |Delta k| = 2k sin(theta_cross/2) from the configured geometry; k for one beam, 0 for a microwave

conv.electric_field_noise.corrected_form: two-sided gives e^2 S_E/(2 m hbar omega); Turchette's arXiv preprint prints Eq. 3 inconsistent by 2 (the published PRA is consistent); the filter-function stack uses two-sided spectra, converted explicitly at the boundary
conv.electric_field_noise.equation: single-sided S_E; Gamma_h = e^2 S_E/(4 m hbar omega)

conv.electric_field_noise_adapter.corrected_form: interpolating a symmetric two-sided tabulation on |omega| is non-monotonic (np.interp then returns a constant, 10x low at DC on a Lorentzian-like table) and clamps at the band edge, which would report 2 S[-1] + white instead of the white level above the band, exactly where the micromotion-sideband heating evaluates S_E
conv.electric_field_noise_adapter.equation: the heating layer takes the NoiseSpectrum RECORD and evaluates 2 S^(2).value(|omega|): the spectrum's own folding onto |omega|, ZERO above the tabulated band (where the density is the white level, which value() adds exactly once), no second white term in NoiseModel.heating_rates_quanta_per_s

conv.entangling_angle.corrected_form: Choi's printed factor 2 holds only for proportional envelopes; Blumel's kernel with target pi/8 must be doubled; Roos's and Kirchmair's pi/8 comes from S without the 1/2 and must not be rescaled
conv.entangling_angle.equation: chi_ij = sum_m eta_im eta_jm int int [Omega_i(t) Omega_j(t') + Omega_j(t) Omega_i(t')] ... with the pair sum over i < j; maximally entangling at chi = pi/4; XX(chi) = exp(-i chi sigma_x sigma_x)

conv.entangling_sign.corrected_form: Waveform.chi_m is SIGNED and, after the exact spot check, carries the measured angle; a solver landing on -pi/4 is not a failure
conv.entangling_sign.equation: a pulse applies exp(+i chi sigma sigma) with chi = sum_m chi_m signed by the detuning side (tones inside the sidebands give chi > 0); XX(chi) = exp(-i chi sigma sigma), so a positive chi is played with a pi on the second ion's tones (GPi(phi + pi) = -GPi(phi)) and a partial angle rescales every amplitude by sqrt((theta/2)/|chi|)

conv.filter_function_normalization.corrected_form: mixing a 1/(2 pi) prefactor with a one-sided integral is a factor 2 in chi; dropping the explicit 1/omega^2 is a factor omega^2; a 1/omega^4 weight appears nowhere
conv.filter_function_normalization.equation: four pieces pinned together: S two-sided in angular frequency with the e^{-i omega t} kernel (per rad/s); prefactor 1/(2 pi) two-sided or 1/pi one-sided; weight 1/omega^2; an explicit -i omega inside R_ij(omega) = -i omega int_0^tau dt R_ij(t) e^{+i omega t}, so only (F = omega^2 |FT[R]|^2, 1/omega^2) and (F = |FT[R]|^2, omega^0) are self-consistent

conv.floquet_phase_origin.corrected_form: the RMP's quantum section and Wineland's trajectory use [1 + (q/2) cos], i nu (1 - q): the same physics half an rf period later
conv.floquet_phase_origin.equation: u_dot(0) = i nu (1 + q) at u(0) = 1 in the adopted sign; C0 = 1 + 3q^2/16 even in q
conv.floquet_phase_origin.symbol: u(t) ~ e^{i nu t}[1 - (q/2) cos omega_rf t]

conv.fock_sum_branches.corrected_form: a joint-space mesolve at dimension 400 would need a 1.6e5 x 1.6e5 Liouvillian with about 6e7 non-zeros per drive operator; Lindblad channels take the trajectory path
conv.fock_sum_branches.equation: the prepared state is diagonal in the computational and Fock bases (pumped populations per ion, thermal weights per carried mode, the frozen modes' Fock states included), so its branches are evolved as pure states with sesolve and recombined with their weights, exact up to the branches below SolverOptions.branch_weight_min (1e-6) whose total weight is reported and renormalized; Diagnostics.trajectories counts the branches

conv.four_ion_gate_local_fixture.corrected_form: the comparison runs at freeze_chi_max_rad = 0.3, where both levels resolve the same single gate mode (|chi| per MS step 0.038 / 0.1078 / 0.1255 / 0.8056 rad on modes 4 to 7 for the (0,1) and (2,3) gates, 0.1251 / 0.1123 / 0.0414 / 0.8395 for (1,2)), JOINT_EXACT at dimension 192 and each step at 48; a hand-built space (modes 6 and 7 at d_m = 12) is not what the criterion selects for either level, and at the default 0.05 rad all four x modes resolve at joint dimension 139968, above the guard, which is why four-ion chains run GATE_LOCAL
conv.four_ion_gate_local_fixture.equation: Section 9.8 row 1: three- AND four-ion circuits of 3 to 5 gates at the resolved-mode sets of Section 9.6 agree in their final probabilities within the residual-displacement bound GATE_LOCAL reports
conv.four_ion_gate_local_fixture.source: the four-ion GHZ circuit (h + three cnots) on the four-ion chain; qutip_trap.run.gate_local

conv.frequencies.corrected_form: papers quote gamma = 2 pi x 19.6 MHz, gamma/2pi = 60 MHz and 19.7 MHz for gamma/2pi interchangeably; the public boundary types are qutip_trap.units.Hz and RadPerS (rad_s_from_hz, hz_from_rad_s), and internal signatures carry the unit in the name (_hz, _rad_s, _hz_per_g, _per_s)
conv.frequencies.equation: internal frequencies angular in rad/s; public API in Hz, converted at the boundary with an explicit 2 pi

conv.frozen_spectator_shot_sample.corrected_form: never the ensemble-mean factor exp[-eta^2(nbar + 1/2)] inside one shot (Section 13, Debye-Waller statistics)
conv.frozen_spectator_shot_sample.equation: a frozen mode's Fock state comes from the sample key frozen_n[m] or, absent that, from a thermal draw at the state's nbar with the keyed stream (sample, 0, 0, 0, 'frozen_n[m]'); it multiplies every drive on the shot by e^{-eta^2/2} L_n(eta^2) and is recorded in the engine report

conv.gate_fidelity_measure.corrected_form: Low, Yoder and Chuang's F = ||U V^dag|| is identically 1 for a qubit under its own Eq. 2 norm and Brown, Harrow and Chuang's 1 - ||V^dag U|| identically 0 for unitaries; both are replaced by F_K
conv.gate_fidelity_measure.equation: for a single-qubit unitary error the internal measure is F_K = (1/4)|Tr(U_id^dag U)|^2, the normalization the composite-pulse library and the Section 6.9 filter functions are built to, which floors at 1/2 for a fully wrong qubit gate; F_C = |Tr(U_id^dag U)|/2 = sqrt(F_K) and F_avg = (2 F_C^2 + 1)/3 = (2 F_K + 1)/3 are conversions, so 1 - F_K = 2(1 - F_C) and 1 - F_avg = (4/3)(1 - F_C) at leading order, and every ingested coefficient is tagged with the measure it was quoted in; at small spectral-norm distance E, 1 - F_C ~ E^2/2 and 1 - F_K ~ E^2; kept separate from conv.rb_error_rate (a decay base) and conv.depolarizing_normalization (a channel rate): this is a unitary overlap
conv.gate_fidelity_measure.source: Kabytayev et al. 2014 Sec. II B; Cummins et al. 2003 Eq. 7; Merrill and Brown Eqs. 10-11; qutip_trap.control.composite

conv.gate_local_discrepancy_has_no_fudge.corrected_form: the comparison holds to discrepancy_bound + dropped_branch_weight exactly, the second term being the weight of the initial-mixture branches JOINT_EXACT did not evolve; there is no further slack
conv.gate_local_discrepancy_has_no_fudge.equation: Section 9.8 row 1: final probabilities agree within the residual-displacement bound GATE_LOCAL reports; disagreement above it fails

conv.gate_local_residual_bound_pre_step.corrected_form: 2 nbar_m + 1 is evaluated at the occupation the tracked model had when the step started, not at the step's output, which would make the bound depend on the gate's own heating
conv.gate_local_residual_bound_pre_step.equation: Section 9.8: the residual-displacement bound sum_m |alpha_m|^2 (2 nbar_m + 1) that GATE_LOCAL reports and the JOINT_EXACT comparison is held to

conv.gate_parameters.corrected_form: the documentation's prose that GPi2 at phi = 0.5 gives R_x(+pi/2) contradicts its own matrix (it is R_x(-pi/2))
conv.gate_parameters.equation: radians internally; IonQ turns at the API boundary (1 turn = 2 pi); phases enter as e^{+-2 pi i phi}, angles as cos(pi theta), sin(pi theta)

conv.ghz_parity_bound.corrected_form: (P_0 + P_1 + C)/2 is an upper bound on the fixed-phase fidelity, not a lower one (the three-ion run: bound 0.9935 against the fixed-phase 0.98520; for the ideal three-ion |GHZ_theta> at theta = 0.7 the bound is 1 and the fixed-phase fidelity cos^2(theta/2) = 0.882421); the 'lower bound' of Wright 2019 concerns an imperfect analysis pulse degrading the measured contrast; phi_0 carries N pi/2 from GPi2's axis and the compiled frames, so only the contrast enters the bound
conv.ghz_parity_bound.equation: P_0 = P(0...0) and P_1 = P(1...1) from the GHZ circuit H, CNOT chain; on fresh shots the parity <prod_q Z_q> after GPi2(phi) on every qubit oscillates as C cos(N phi + phi_0) with C = 2 |rho_{0...0, 1...1}| (only the sigma_+^{ox N} term carries e^{i N phi}), fitted from at least four phases over one period 2 pi/N; since P_0 and P_1 are the diagonal elements, (P_0 + P_1 + C)/2 = max_theta <GHZ_theta| rho |GHZ_theta> with |GHZ_theta> = (|0...0> + e^{i theta}|1...1>)/sqrt 2, an equality with the phase-optimised fidelity; the simulator reports GHZResult.register_fidelity_max_phase (what the bound estimates) and GHZResult.register_fidelity (against the fixed-phase target) beside it, with the shot-noise uncertainties of P_0, P_1 and C combined in quadrature
conv.ghz_parity_bound.source: Sackett et al. 2000; Leibfried et al. 2005; Wright et al. 2019; qutip_trap.benchmarks.ghz

conv.gradient_drive.corrected_form: r_0 with the total two-ion mass is right: on an antisymmetric mode w_{i,m} = +-2 Omega_g exactly with Omega_g = (r_0/4) grad(B)(d omega_0/dB) and r_0 = sqrt(hbar/(2 M_total omega_m)); a gradient gate needs a field-sensitive qubit (d omega_0/dB vanishes at a clock point, so Srinivas's |3,3> <-> |2,2> of 25Mg+), and the linear AM closure algebra does not apply because the force is a Bessel function of the tone amplitude (Omega_g J_2(4 Omega_mu/delta)): Srinivas's Walsh sign modulation is the applicable family, played through the sigma_z spin-echo path, and the closure solvers do not cover it
conv.gradient_drive.equation: the near-field microwave-gradient drive is device-level: GradientField carries the electrodes' oscillating gradient amplitude d(B_g . B_hat)/dr (T/m), its frequency omega_g, its axis, the two microwave tones' field amplitude B_1 and the gradient's phase; derive_gradient_drive returns Omega_mu = (B_x/2 hbar)<dn|mu_x|up> from the magnetic-dipole coupling, d omega_0/dB from the hyperfine-Zeeman diagonalization, and the per-(ion, mode) force w_{i,m} = (1/2)(d omega_0/dB) grad(B)(r_hat . e_hat_m) c_{i,m} sqrt(hbar/(2 m_i omega_m)) from the mode's mass-weighted pattern; the builder's 'gradient' branch adds sum_{i,m} w_{i,m} sigma_z^i (a_m + a_m^dag) cos(omega_g t + phi_g) beside the two microwave tones (BuilderOptions.gradient_form = 'bare', the default, so that J_2(4 Omega_mu/delta) and the J_0 = 0 decoupling emerge from the exact dynamics) or the eliminated (w_{i,m}/2) J_2 sigma_z^i (a_m e^{i(omega_g + 2 delta) t} + h.c.) alone ('dressed', recorded in approximations)
conv.gradient_drive.source: Srinivas et al., Nature 597, 209 (2021) Eq. 1; qutip_trap.light.microwave; qutip_trap.dynamics.hamiltonian

conv.hamiltonian_fingerprint_carries_the.corrected_form: without device.hash() one engine over two devices differing only in beam 0's wavelength (355 nm -> 344.35 nm) would serve the first device's propagator for the second on an internal-state-only space, a silent 1.5e-4 error in P1[0]
conv.hamiltonian_fingerprint_carries_the.equation: the fingerprint digest is (device.hash(), the space, the mode frequencies, the segment times, the pulses' sampled tones, the frozen Fock states, the noise sample's values and OU grids, the qubit shifts, the BuilderOptions with kernel normalized to auto)

conv.heating_master_equation.corrected_form: the journal prints 2 a rho^dagger a^dagger, a typesetting artifact absent from both arXiv versions
conv.heating_master_equation.equation: rates Gamma(N_bar + 1) on a and Gamma N_bar on a^dagger; a quoted heating rate is d<n>/dt at n = 0, i.e. Gamma N_bar; thermal diffusion Gamma(2 N_bar + 1)

conv.heating_rate_meaning.corrected_form: Trout's symmetric infinite-temperature pair {sqrt(n_dot) a, sqrt(n_dot) a^dag} is the N_bar >> 1 limit, never to be imported with a finite N_bar
conv.heating_rate_meaning.equation: a quoted rate is d<n>/dt at n = 0, i.e. Gamma N_bar; thermal diffusion is Gamma(2 N_bar + 1); n_dot ~ omega^-(alpha+1) when S_E ~ omega^-alpha; the coherence of (|n0> + |m0>)/sqrt 2 decays at Gamma_h (n0 + m0 + 1)

conv.heavy_output_criterion.equation: square circuits of width n and depth d = n, every layer a uniform random permutation and a Haar-random SU(4) (Mezzadri's QR construction) on each of the floor(n/2) pairs, adjacent local unitaries merged per qubit; the heavy outputs are the strings whose ideal probability exceeds the median of the ideal distribution; h_U is the measured fraction of shots on them; the width passes when the mean of h_U over circuits clears 2/3 by two sigma and the run has at least the protocol's 100 circuits, the confidence being Appendix C Eq. (32), [n_h - z sqrt(n_h (n_s - n_h/n_c))]/(n_c n_s) > 2/3 with z = 2, which with h = n_h/(n_c n_s) reduces identically to mean - 2 sigma > 2/3 with the per-circuit binomial sigma = sqrt(h(1 - h)/n_c); the standard error of the mean is reported beside it (QVResult.standard_error_of_the_mean) and is never the criterion, and QVResult.threshold_cleared carries the confidence half alone, so a run below 100 circuits says so and clears no quantum volume; under a depolarizing composition h_pred = h_ideal (1 - eps) + eps/2
conv.heavy_output_criterion.source: Cross, Bishop, Sheldon, Nation and Gambetta, PRA 100, 032328 (2019), Appendix C Eq. (32); qutip_trap.benchmarks.volume
conv.heavy_output_criterion.symbol: mean(h_U) - 2 sqrt(h(1 - h)/n_c) > 2/3 over n_c >= 100 circuits

conv.hyperfine_dipole_element.corrected_form: the ingest test reproduces the 171Yb+ 1/3 : 2/3 branching and the 50.8 mW/cm^2 I_sat
conv.hyperfine_dipole_element.equation: <F mF|d_q|F' mF'> = <J||d||J'> (-1)^{F'+J+1+I} sqrt((2F'+1)(2J+1)) {J J' 1; F' F I} (-1)^{F'-1+mF} sqrt(2F+1) (F' 1 F; mF' q -mF); q = m_lower - m_upper

conv.hyperfine_factors.corrected_form: one 'hyperfine factor' used in both roles is off by (2F+1)(2J'+1)/((2F'+1)(2J+1))
conv.hyperfine_factors.equation: S_FF' = (2F'+1)(2J+1){J J' 1; F' F I}^2 summing to one over excited F' (absorption); b(F'->F) = (2F+1)(2J'+1){...}^2 summing to one over ground F (emission)

conv.improved_sampling_single_segment.corrected_form: the weights are McResult.deterministic_weights (one per initial state) and runs_weights (per stochastic trajectory, matched to the keyed seeds through res.seeds); the single-segment restriction is this engine's: applied per segment the no-jump/jump split gives 2^n weighted pure members that cannot be merged on the trajectory path, and pruning them at branch_weight_min would discard the jump weight (per-segment jump probability 1e-5 on the two-ion fixture); a per-segment keyed resampling to ntraj members would be the bounded fix and is not implemented
conv.improved_sampling_single_segment.equation: with improved_sampling=True QuTiP evolves the no-jump trajectory once as a deterministic member of weight p_no-jump and gives the ntraj stochastic trajectories the residual weight, so the engine's per-member weights are res.deterministic_weights for res.deterministic_trajectories and res.runs_weights for res.trajectories; drawing uniformly from the stored trajectories instead biases every per-shot observable by p_no-jump. The engine uses it when the trajectory path is entered exactly ONCE in a schedule (SolverOptions.improved_sampling, default True); a multi-segment schedule keeps uniform-weight trajectories and says so in the run's notes

conv.ladder_operators.corrected_form: Brownnutt arXiv v1 prints a with sqrt(hbar m omega); Ozeri 2007 and Baldwin 2021 put a factor 4 under the root
conv.ladder_operators.equation: x = x0 (a + a^dagger), x0 = sqrt(hbar/(2 m omega))

conv.lamb_dicke.corrected_form: Sorensen-Molmer's and Leung's per-ion COM eta already contains 1/sqrt N; Srinivas puts the total two-ion mass inside r0
conv.lamb_dicke.equation: eta_{i,m} = (Delta k . e_m) c_{i,m} sqrt(hbar/(2 m_i omega_m)) with the ion's own mass and the mass-weighted unit-norm eigenvector component; C0 applied once in Crystal.lamb_dicke
conv.lamb_dicke.source: Wineland 1998 Eq. 33; Monroe 2020; Home 2013 Eq. 19; Morigi-Walther Eq. 12

conv.large_mode_atol_floor.corrected_form: max(atol, 1e-8) would clamp a deliberately tightened atol back to 1e-8 in a Section 5.5 convergence run and report a spuriously small change; the d_m = 121, 151 and 201 cases integrate on the first rung at the keyed 1e-8, and a stiff abort at d_m = 121 with atol 1e-10 does not reproduce on a one-mode detuned spin-dependent force
conv.large_mode_atol_floor.equation: the keying of Section 5.3 relaxes atol to LARGE_MODE_ATOL = 1e-8 above LARGE_MODE_DIMENSION = 100 when and only when the caller left SolverOptions.atol at its 1e-10 default; a deliberately tightened or loosened atol is used as given. dynamics.evolve.convergence_check(run, options) is the named-observable companion to hilbert.truncation.halving_test: it runs a closure at both tolerance pairs and reports max_t |delta p| per observable with a summary string, and it is applied to the Section 9.2 carrier and blue-sideband fixtures (both converge below 1e-6)
conv.large_mode_atol_floor.symbol: atol = 1e-8 above d_m ~ 100, only when atol is the default

conv.level_a_rates_participation.corrected_form: the W(Delta -+ nu) closed form with each beam shifted in turn is the weak-drive alternative, refused above Omega/Gamma = 0.1 (Section 4.2.8 vii); a mode whose projection on every cooling beam is below (k_hat . e_m)^2 = 1e-2 raises UncooledModeError instead of returning a steady state (Section 4.2)
conv.level_a_rates_participation.equation: per illuminated ion and mode the phonon rates come from the dipole-force spectrum of the ion's internal steady state under all its beams (exact in the saturation) plus the per-channel emission diffusion, with the mass-weighted participation folded into the zero-point length x0_eff = |c| sqrt(hbar/(2 m_i omega)); the mode rate carries W_k = sum_i c_{i,k}^2 and nbar = sum heating/(sum cooling - sum heating) is participation independent when the ions see one intensity (a two-ion COM mode: nbar equal to the single ion's to 1e-6, the rate halved when one ion is illuminated)

conv.light_shift_force.corrected_form: for a force on one level only (weights (-2, 0), the 40Ca+ S1/2-D5/2 qubit under 398 nm light, or Baldwin's |up>) the single-qubit sigma_z phase is four times the two-body angle, which the spin echo of Section 4.4.4 cancels; the sign of a sigma_z force follows the detuning side alone (no phase flip)
conv.light_shift_force.equation: Omega_gg = sum_e conj(Omega^(2)_eg) Omega^(1)_eg/(2 Delta_e) for each qubit level g under the beam pair; the light-shift drive is (1/2) sum_tones Omega_LS e^{-i(mu t - phi)} [w_dn P_0 + w_up P_1] (x) D + h.c. with Omega_LS = (Omega_upup - Omega_dndn)/2 and weights (Omega_dndn, Omega_upup)/Omega_LS (differing by exactly 2): Zhu's hbar Omega_j cos(Delta k . q_j + mu t) sigma_z^j plus the spin-independent force; the same beams' Raman coupling Omega_R rotates at mu - omega_0 and is kept unless its excitation is below 1e-12
conv.light_shift_force.source: Wineland 2003 (two-photon coupling with g' = g); Zhu-Monroe-Duan 2006 Eq. 2; Ballance 2016; Baldwin 2021

conv.linewidth_gamma.corrected_form: an assertion checks Gamma/2pi equals the quoted MHz
conv.linewidth_gamma.equation: Gamma is the angular population decay rate of the upper level's TOTAL decay; gamma_hz = Gamma/2pi; the partial rate into a lower level is Gamma x branching

conv.mass_ion.corrected_form: eta(N = 17) rounds to 0.0267 at 171 u and 0.0268 at the ion mass
conv.mass_ion.equation: Species.mass_u is the ION mass, the cited atomic mass minus one electron mass (171Yb+: 170.93578 u from 170.9363302 u); the Lamb-Dicke anchor must state its mass

conv.mathieu_sign.corrected_form: Wineland 1998 and Berkeland 1998 use +2q cos (a half-period shift); factor-4 q definitions elsewhere; House 2008 has Q = -q and prints its first-order matrix with the wrong sign
conv.mathieu_sign.equation: d^2x/dxi^2 + [a - 2q cos 2xi] x = 0, xi = omega_rf t/2, a = 4Z|e|U alpha/(m omega_rf^2), q = 2Z|e|U~ alpha'/(m omega_rf^2)

conv.mcsolve_weight_attributes.corrected_form: no attribute deterministic_weight_info exists in QuTiP 5.3.1
conv.mcsolve_weight_attributes.equation: with improved_sampling=True mcsolve evolves one deterministic no-jump member (McResult.deterministic_trajectories, weight McResult.deterministic_weights[0]) and gives the stochastic trajectories the residual weights McResult.runs_weights; shots are drawn from that weighted mixture

conv.mean_count_curve.corrected_form: the fit is degenerate at bin-time windows (tens of us: R_b unconstrained, the least-squares returned 1e4 Hz); it needs windows long against 1/R_d and 1/R_b, as Noek's 60 ms, so calibrate_detection draws a separate long record set for the fit
conv.mean_count_curve.equation: the calibration fit for (εR_o, R_d, R_b) from bright-prepared records; equals the exact chain's mean when only R_d and R_b act
conv.mean_count_curve.source: Noek 2013 Eq. 4 with ṗ_1 = R_b p_0 - R_d p_1

conv.mg25_no_measured_g_j.corrected_form: 9Be+'s measured g_J = 2.00226 is not a 25Mg+ value (g_J = 2.000 moves the 212.78 G clock point to 213.025 G), and g_J is not back-solved from the ratio and a tabulated mu_I (the two shielding conventions give 2.0045 or fail the 9Be+ cross-check at 4e-4), so the 25Mg+ table stays incomplete
conv.mg25_no_measured_g_j.equation: no measured absolute g_J of the 25Mg+ ground state exists: both measurements servo the field to the electronic transition and determine only the ratio g_I/g_J = 9.299484(75)e-5 (Itano and Wineland 1981) or 9.299308313(60)e-5 (Brewer et al. 2019), which the table stores
conv.mg25_no_measured_g_j.source: Itano and Wineland, Phys. Rev. A 24, 1364 (1981); Brewer et al., Phys. Rev. A 100, 013409 (2019); qutip_trap.species.mg25

conv.micromotion_amplitude_convention.corrected_form: Blakestad's zone-E numbers mix the conventions (68 nm peak against 47 nm rms); an unsigned +(1/2) q u_0 is the other rf phase origin and inverts every micromotion-sideband phase and the sign of the rf-photon correlation servo step while leaving the fitted null and J_0 unchanged
conv.micromotion_amplitude_convention.equation: declared explicitly: SIGNED peak amplitude u_1 = -(1/2) q u_0 for the stray-field term, the minus sign forced by conv.floquet_phase_origin (the adopted a - 2q cos 2xi origin makes the in-phase micromotion a contraction, x_mu = -(q_x/2) x_sec cos omega_rf t); beta = delta_k . u_1 is signed too, so sign(beta_ip) = -sign(q_x E_x) and it steps by pi across the compensated shim; the in-phase (nullable) and out-of-phase ((1/4) q R alpha phi_ac, not nullable) indices never collapse into one number; total adds in quadrature, and the builder consumes the pair as (hypot(ip, op), rf phase + -atan2(op, ip))

conv.micromotion_correction.corrected_form: the RMP's (1 + q/2)^-1 is the u(0) = 1 normalization at one rf phase, an rf-clock artifact
conv.micromotion_correction.equation: eta_eff = eta C0, C0 the e^{i nu t} Fourier coefficient of the exact Floquet function normalized by Im(u* u_dot) = nu: C0 = 1 + 3q^2/16 + O(q^4) (1.007741 at q = 0.2)

conv.mode_classes_and_tolerances.corrected_form: no source gives a value for the freezing tolerance of the residual displacement: 1e-4 is a default, an approximation of the truncation kind reported per run
conv.mode_classes_and_tolerances.equation: per mode, from the Section 4.4.3 integrals of every played waveform with the prepared occupations: dropped when |alpha|^2 (2 nbar + 1) < 1e-6 and |chi| < 1e-4; frozen when |alpha|^2 (2 nbar + 1) < SolverOptions.freeze_alpha_max (1e-4) and |chi| < freeze_chi_max_rad (0.05); resolved otherwise, with the cap from the loop radius eta Omega/epsilon, the occupation and the Section 5.1.1 margin; a frozen mode's chi is absorbed by the exact spot check on the reduced space (the frozen run is calibrated to the same angle) and reported; modes only carrier pulses touch are frozen

conv.mode_dimension_max.corrected_form: a clamp never narrows the declared expected occupation range (which would run the Section 5.1.1 oracle and the Section 5.5 margin check over less than the physics): it emits a SpaceSelection.notes entry naming the mode, the d the rule asked for and the clamped range; a Doppler-cooled nbar ~ 20 mode at eta = 0.1 needs d = 156 for a boundary population below 1e-4
conv.mode_dimension_max.equation: the cap rule takes the populated range of the thermal mode displaced by the loop radius at the boundary threshold, plus the Section 5.1.1 margin for the mode's eta, clamped to mode_dimension_max (default 64)

conv.mode_eigenvector_gauge.corrected_form: James's Table 2 eigenvectors are sign-consistent with the closed forms
conv.mode_eigenvector_gauge.equation: orthonormal, axial eigenvalues increasing, last component positive; transverse families numbered ascending in frequency, so the COM is the last transverse mode

conv.mode_index.corrected_form: an index is never the eigensolver output order, a frequency order across families or a (family, index) pair
conv.mode_index.equation: every mode index is a position in Crystal.modes, ordered axial, transverse_1, transverse_2, ascending frequency within a family; eigenvectors unit norm, last component positive
