conv.motion_phase_default.corrected_form: the sine beat-note convention of Section 4.4.3 (phi_b - phi_r = pi, force zero at t = 0) is for the closed forms only: played literally at Omega/mu = 0.1 it tilts the axis by 0.202 rad and leaks sin^2 psi = 3.8 % into |du>, |ud> (concurrence 0.9597 against 0.9999 with equal phases); the kernels carry phi_m explicitly, and Choi's sin(mu t) e^{i omega t} is their phi_m = pi/2 case
conv.motion_phase_default.equation: the played waveforms default to equal tone phases (phi_b = phi_r, the force Omega cos(mu t)); the carrier Omega cos(mu t - phi_m) rotates the spin at F(t) = (2 Omega/mu)[sin(mu t - phi_m) + sin phi_m], whose mean tilts the force axis by psi = (2 Omega/mu) sin phi_m

conv.motional_dephasing_from_rf_noise.corrected_form: the tabulated band of the same spectrum is a common-mode fractional trajectory of the transverse modes, never M independent offsets (Section 6.2)
conv.motional_dephasing_from_rf_noise.equation: a white fractional rf-amplitude density S_V gives a white mode-frequency density omega_m^2 S_V and the coherence of |n> + |n'> decays at (n - n')^2/tau; the axial (dc) family does not follow the rf amplitude
conv.motional_dephasing_from_rf_noise.source: the Section 13 motional-dephasing operator with omega_m proportional to V_rf for the transverse families; qutip_trap.noise.model

conv.ms_closure.corrected_form: the closure is not 1/(4 sqrt K), which is a factor-2 force error; Roos's Omega_c = |eps|/(4 eta) reads |eps|/(2 eta) in this Omega
conv.ms_closure.equation: the force on S_y is -(hbar eta Omega/2)(a^dagger e^{i eps t} + h.c.) for the per-tone Omega; closure eta Omega/eps = 1/(2 sqrt K) in every spin normalization; targets -pi/2 on J_y^2, -pi/8 on S_y^2, pi/4 on sigma_y sigma_y

conv.mu_i_shielding_convention.corrected_form: the 43Ca+ value is the free-ion moment Hanley et al. print to 9e-6, the moment a trapped-ion Breit-Rabi Hamiltonian takes, not a fitted constant; mixing the conventions between species is a 0.2 to 0.25 % error in g_I
conv.mu_i_shielding_convention.equation: the tables carry mu_I in three conventions, each declared per table: 9Be+ -1.177432 mu_N diamagnetically corrected (Dickopf 2024's g_I gives -1.1774316344; the uncorrected NMR value is -1.17449(2), 0.25 % away), 25Mg+ -0.85545 mu_N uncorrected (Alder and Yu 1951 via Stone; Stone's corrected recommendation is -0.85533(3)), 43Ca+ -1.315350(9) mu_N free-ion (Hanley et al. 2021; Stone's bare-nucleus value is -1.31733(6))
conv.mu_i_shielding_convention.source: Stone INDC(NDS)-0794; Dickopf et al., Nature 632, 757 (2024); Hanley et al., arXiv:2105.10352

conv.native_ms_matrix.equation: MS(phi0, phi1, theta) = exp[-i pi theta GPi(phi0) (x) GPi(phi1)] with theta in turns in [0, 0.25]; GPi(phi) = [[0, e^{-2 pi i phi}], [e^{2 pi i phi}, 0]]; GPi2(phi) = (1/sqrt 2)[[1, -i e^{-2 pi i phi}], [-i e^{2 pi i phi}, 1]]; ZZ(theta) = diag(e^{-i pi theta}, e^{i pi theta}, e^{i pi theta}, e^{-i pi theta}); XX(chi) = MS(0, 0, theta) with chi = pi theta
conv.native_ms_matrix.source: IonQ documentation; qiskit-ionq, ionq-core-python and PennyLane-IonQ client code

conv.no_stark_imbalance.corrected_form: the imbalance is carried by the two legs' amplitudes, not a CalibrationTable entry, and the closed forms ignore it (one amplitude per ion and segment), so a waveform with imbalance != 0 carries the balanced pulse's chi_m and alpha_m
conv.no_stark_imbalance.equation: the solvers accept an imbalance that splits the two legs' amplitudes, and no caller passes a non-zero value: the compensation law xi = (delta eta^2/|eps|)(phi/pi), the differential shift delta_ac^(C) = 2(Omega_r^2 - Omega_b^2)/delta = -8 Omega^2 xi/delta, the delta^(SB) = (eps/2) xi n term that breaks thermal-state operation and the third-tone alternative are not implemented

conv.noise_provenance.equation: one tag per apparatus per rate ('author year, species, N ions'); NoiseModel.apparatus() unions the tags of every NON-QUIET rate (a zero rate contributes nothing to a budget and so no apparatus), undeclared_rate_count() counts the non-zero rates with no tag, and provenance_sentence() is emitted into Diagnostics.approximations whenever either is non-empty

conv.noise_routing.corrected_form: no heuristic on a spectrum's shape decides its route: the two fields declare the split; a grid that cannot resolve the band refuses with the remedy (declare the band above it as white_level)
conv.noise_routing.equation: a NoiseSpectrum's tabulated band is synthesized per dynamical sample on a fixed grid (x(t) = sum_k sqrt(S(omega_k) d omega_k/pi)[a_k cos + b_k sin], <x^2> = (1/pi) int S d omega); its white_level is a Lindblad rate; Drift records are OU chains over the shot clock; collisions are Poisson events per shot

conv.nuclear_g_sign.corrected_form: Harty's g_I^(N) = mu_I/(I mu_N) with a minus sign and Langer's g_I = -mu_I/(I mu_B) with a plus are self-consistent alternatives that must not be mixed: 83.76 kHz and 0.207 G off for 43Ca+
conv.nuclear_g_sign.equation: g_I = -(mu_I/(I mu_N))(m_e/m_p), so H_Z = mu_B (g_J J_z + g_I I_z) B/hbar with one sign for both; 43Ca+ g_I = +2.0467e-4 from mu_I = -1.31535 mu_N

conv.oracle_margin_rule.corrected_form: a fatal oracle at small caps would defeat the cap-raising retries of Section 5.5, which start from a deliberately small cap
conv.oracle_margin_rule.equation: HilbertSpace.displacement_factor asserts the interior elements against the analytic oracle to interior_tolerance(margin, eta) (the table row d = 2 margin, log-interpolated, floored at 1e-12) whenever the margin above the declared range is at least 4 levels; below the table's smallest row the difference is reported by oracle_status and the boundary monitor governs; required margins 6/10/20 at eta 0.1/0.5/1.0 are stored as an interpolated fixture

conv.played_chain.corrected_form: playing the table's Rabi frequency, Stark shift and crosstalk as the physics would make a miscalibrated entry error-free by construction
conv.played_chain.equation: every pulse the scheduler emits carries the table's beliefs (Drive.programmed); the engine converts a requested Rabi frequency through the device's derived map divided by the calibrated one, the light shift to the derived shift at the played intensity (delta_derived sum_tones (Omega_phys/Omega_derived)^p), the crosstalk to the derived ratios of the listed neighbours; the identity for a surrogate table (seeds = derived values). The conversion applies to the kinds whose rf-power-to-Omega map the light layer derives from the beams and the atomic structure (raman, optical_E1, optical_E2); a microwave, light-shift (Section 4.4.4) or microwave-gradient drive is played exactly as requested, so a miscalibrated table produces no over-rotation, detuning or crosstalk error for it, although Section 7.10 exempts nothing and a light-shift drive's Omega is derivable from the beams (open)

conv.pm_solver.corrected_form: SegmentedEnvelope carries an optional per-segment phase offset in the two legs' half-difference (the spin phase, the half-sum, never moves); Milne's N + 1 phase segments need a time-symmetric profile this solver does not impose (at 3 segments |alpha| ~ 1e-2 on the two-ion fixture, where Choi's 2N + 1 = 5 close both modes to 3e-17), and the motion phase is the modulation parameter, so Roos's spin-axis tilt is intrinsic (1.8e-2 leakage against 4.7e-4 for FM and 4.7e-7 for Fourier AM)
conv.pm_solver.equation: no source of Section 4.4.3 gives a PM solver (AM: Zhu, Choi; FM: Leung; AMFM: Blumel), so the family implemented is the piecewise-constant per-segment motion phase at fixed amplitude and beat note, alpha_{i,m} = i eta_{i,m} Omega sum_k e^{i phi_k} F_k^{(m)} with the same symmetrized double integral and the phases inside, solved by least squares like the FM vertices and scaled to |chi| = chi_target; the three sources above are its provenance
conv.pm_solver.source: Milne et al., PRApplied 13, 024022 (2020); Green and Biercuk, PRL 114, 120502 (2015); Lu et al., Nature 572, 363 (2019)

conv.polarization_components.corrected_form: Steck's tables list sigma+ under q = -1: the helicity and operator-index labels are interchanged there
conv.polarization_components.equation: eps = sum_q eps_q e_q about B, e_{+-1} = -+(x +- i y)/sqrt 2, e_0 = z; helicity q_gamma = +1 (sigma+), 0 (pi), -1 (sigma-) for absorption |F mF> -> |F' mF + q_gamma>; operator index q_op = m_lower - m_upper = -q_gamma

conv.preparation_single_species_f0.corrected_form: standard_recipe covers only a single-species crystal with an F = 0 qubit level; an optical, Zeeman or mixed-species qubit needs an explicit Device.preparation (ca40_optical_recipe is the worked example)
conv.preparation_single_species_f0.equation: standard_recipe builds a recipe only for a SINGLE-SPECIES crystal (prep/recipe.py _structure) whose qubit's lower level is an F = 0 hyperfine state (its pump is the F = I + 1/2 -> F' = I + 1/2 line of the cycling transition); every other qubit - optical, Zeeman, and any mixed-species crystal - needs an explicit Device.preparation, which run() honours. device/presets.ca40_optical_recipe is the worked example for a 40Ca+ optical qubit: 397 nm Doppler cooling at -Gamma/2 along the oblique path with the 866 nm D3/2 repump, no sideband stage, and a pump into S1/2 mJ = -1/2 by 397 nm sigma- light along B with the same repump (the I = 0 analogue of the 171Yb+ F = 1 -> F' = 1 pump)

conv.preparation_stage_order.corrected_form: not the reverse order (pump first); run.prepare takes the recipe the Device carries
conv.preparation_stage_order.equation: PreparationSequence refuses a sequence that does not start with Doppler cooling, a sub-Doppler stage with no Doppler precooling before it, and a pump followed by a cooling stage with no later pump; the hand-off State takes each mode's nbar from the LAST stage that addressed it and each ion's internal state from its last pump (or an explicit state for an unpumped coolant/qubit)

conv.pseudopotential_error_estimate.corrected_form: 'in units of the mode spacing' is read as the ion spacing, the small parameter of Kaufmann's mechanism; a single ion gets a note instead of a number
conv.pseudopotential_error_estimate.equation: Device.derived() reports pseudopotential_error = max_i |u_1,i| / min_ij |r_i - r_j|, with u_1 = -(q/2) u_0 the signed excess-micromotion amplitude and the denominator the smallest inter-ion distance: the fractional rf modulation of the Coulomb curvature (~1/r^3, so delta K/K ~ 3 |u_1|/s) that makes the pseudopotential modes of 4.1.3 inexact off the rf null. It is exactly 0 for a chain on the null with no stray field. Also reported: ion_height_m and trap_depth_ev on the surface path (4.1.6 'the module reports h and the trap depth with every device that uses it') and second_order_doppler[i] (4.1.1 'reports the implied second-order Doppler shift for completeness')

conv.quadrupole_coupling.corrected_form: q = Delta m elsewhere; unit-normalized rank-2 tensors (sqrt(3/2) too large); r^2 Y_2m (sqrt(4 pi/5) too large); the lower-level 2j + 1 (sqrt 3 too small); air wavelengths in James's calcium panel and Roos's table; the Boulder Omega is half
conv.quadrupole_coupling.equation: Omega_{mm'} = (e E_0 k/(2 hbar)) |<S||r^2 C^(2)||D>| |Lambda(m, m')| |g^(q)| with q = m - m', k = 2 pi/lambda_vac the single beam's wavenumber, C^(2)_q = sqrt(4 pi/5) Y_2q (Racah), rank-2 tensors normalized to 2/3, A = c alpha k^5 |<||>|^2/(15 (2 j' + 1)) with the upper j'; carrier pi pulse at t = pi/Omega

conv.qubit_dephasing_from_field_noise.corrected_form: the white field level is a device declaration (NoiseSpectrum.white_level), never inferred from the band
conv.qubit_dephasing_from_field_noise.equation: S_delta = (2 pi d1)^2 S_B (d1 in Hz/G, S_B in G^2/(rad/s)); gamma_phi = S_delta/2; the Ramsey coherence decays as e^{-gamma_phi t}
conv.qubit_dephasing_from_field_noise.source: the Section 13 chain H_deph = b sigma_z, b = pi delta nu, S_b = S_delta/4, L = sqrt(gamma/2) sigma_z; qutip_trap.noise.model

conv.qubit_dephasing_operator.corrected_form: sources that write the decay rate as 2/T2 use another operator normalization
conv.qubit_dephasing_operator.equation: coherence decays at gamma_phi, so gamma_phi = 1/T2 for the white component; a measured T2 is split into quasi-static (Gaussian) and white (exponential) parts before use

conv.rabi_frequency.corrected_form: Wineland 1998, Monroe 1995 and Blumel 2021 use P = sin^2(Omega t), half the usual Rabi frequency
conv.rabi_frequency.equation: H = (hbar Omega/2) sigma_+ e^{...} + h.c., carrier pi pulse at Omega t = pi

conv.rabi_from_intensity.corrected_form: Noek's s in the (Gamma/6, 2/3) detection form is I/(3 I_sat), the exact four-level result with one polarization share per sublevel (Section 8.1)
conv.rabi_from_intensity.equation: E_0 = sqrt(2 I/(eps_0 c)); on the cycling transition this reduces to Omega = Gamma sqrt(I/(2 I_sat)) and s = I/I_sat = 2 Omega^2/Gamma^2 there only

conv.rayleigh_dissipator.equation: dissipator prefactor Gamma_el/4 while the coherence decays at Gamma_el/2, both consistent; Raman operators sqrt(Gamma_du)|u><d| carry the plain rate

conv.rb_error_rate.corrected_form: the entanglement infidelity is not the RB error rate (1.5x at n = 1 and 1.25x at n = 2 too large); Wright's 'p is the gate fidelity'; Chen's Eq. 3 conflates decay bases with rates and prints a singular matrix
conv.rb_error_rate.equation: an RB decay F(m) = A p^m + B reports r = (1 - p)(2^n - 1)/2^n, the average error per Clifford ((1 - p)/2 for one qubit, (3/4)(1 - p) for two); (4^n - 1)(1 - p)/4^n is the entanglement infidelity of the depolarizing channel with the same p and is reported under that name (rb_error_per_clifford and depolarizing_entanglement_infidelity; RBResult.error_per_clifford)
conv.rb_error_rate.source: Magesan, Gambetta and Emerson 2011; Wright et al. 2019; Chen et al. 2023

conv.readout_chain_exact.corrected_form: the single-jump forms are the small-k-tau oracles: with one transition rate the exponential equals them to 1e-13; with both rates it differs by the second jump (1e-3 relative at Crain's 22 us). mcsolve needs the problem in units of the window (its collapse-time search has an absolute time tolerance)
conv.readout_chain_exact.equation: the count distribution over a window is one matrix exponential of the augmented generator (blocks Q - diag(lambda) with diag(lambda) one block up, an absorbing overflow block); the fast path samples the chain exactly (Gillespie) with Poisson counts at the piecewise rates, the trajectory path runs mcsolve on the class space with a photon-counting collapse operator
conv.readout_chain_exact.source: Markov-modulated Poisson process on the bright/dark/shelf chain; Crain Eq. 1 and Acton Eqs. 5-6 as its single-jump limits; qutip_trap.readout.detection

conv.readout_crosstalk_added_counts.corrected_form: the product POVM is exact only at zero crosstalk: at 4 % leakage a dark 171Yb+ ion beside a bright one under the zero-threshold SNSPD protocol reads bright 34 % of the time (0.42 leaked counts in 22 us), the bounded, reported discrepancy of Section 9.5
conv.readout_crosstalk_added_counts.equation: a bright neighbour's leaked light is ADDED COUNTS on its neighbours at the configured PSF fraction AND extra off-resonant pumping on their chains (the 'depumping-reduced N' half, anchor.m5.crosstalk_depumping); the register confusion at configured crosstalk is factored by neighbour range (per-ion conditional tables over the ion's own LEVEL and its neighbours' start classes, exact for per-ion decisions on additive light with the neighbours' pumping frozen at their start class), dense to N = 12
conv.readout_crosstalk_added_counts.source: Wineland 1998 (degraded discrimination, not a changed eta_d); Burrell 2010 (PSF overlap); Acton 2006 Eq. 22 with the corrected I_sat

conv.readout_detected_line.corrected_form: summing every non-sink decay line would count a 40Ca+ repump's 866 nm photons, making R_o high by exactly 1 + Gamma(D3/2<-P1/2)/Gamma(S1/2<-P1/2) = 1.0638 and the whole budget with it; a repump's manifold enters the model only when the device has a beam on that line, since without it the metastable level is a dead end whose lifetime is the slowest Liouvillian mode
conv.readout_detected_line.equation: epsilon_sys carries exactly one epsilon_filter and an interference filter passes one wavelength, so R_o counts photons on the species' CYCLING line only: detection_rates_for_ion passes line = '<lower><-<upper>' of species.cycling, rates_from_bloch derives the single non-sink line when the build has one and REFUSES to guess when it has several, and line=ALL_LINES is an explicit all-line diagnostic (the total scattering rate W(Delta) of Section 4.2.2), never a detected rate
conv.readout_detected_line.symbol: R_det = eps_sys R_o on ONE line

conv.readout_polarity_scheme.corrected_form: the qubit label carries no polarity; the code refuses a scheme in which no level fluoresces
conv.readout_polarity_scheme.equation: bright/dark is a property of the readout SCHEME stored as an enum: 171Yb+ direct fluorescence has |1> = F = 1 bright; the 40Ca+ optical qubit has |0> = S1/2 bright and |1> = D5/2 the shelf; shelving transfer is a START distribution per level, so Pi_dark = sum_l p_l |l><l| is not rank one
conv.readout_polarity_scheme.source: Myerson 2008; Christensen 2020; Harty 2014 (direct fluorescence and shelving invert the polarity within one paper)

conv.result_bit_order.corrected_form: PennyLane reverses the order to big-endian (checked against the client sources)
conv.result_bit_order.equation: qubit 0 is the least-significant bit of the decimal histogram key; {"5": 0.5, "7": 0.5} on three qubits <-> bitstrings 101, 111; shots ["6","1","0","7"] <-> 110, 001, 000, 111
conv.result_bit_order.source: IonQ OpenAPI v0.4; qiskit-ionq and PennyLane-IonQ client code

conv.rf_amplitude_pseudopotential.corrected_form: reading the stored peak as rms doubles the depth and inflates every rf-set secular frequency by sqrt 2, and as peak-to-peak quarters the depth and halves those frequencies
conv.rf_amplitude_pseudopotential.equation: V_rf is the PEAK of a cos(Omega_rf t) drive; psi = Q^2|E|^2/(4 m Omega^2) in joules (eV at the boundary)
conv.rf_amplitude_pseudopotential.source: House; Wesenberg; Chiaverini; Madsen; Home; Kielpinski

conv.saturation_ceiling.corrected_form: not the two-level Lorentzian's Gamma/2 on a degenerate manifold, nor a 'naive four-level' 1/2 for the 171Yb+ detection line
conv.saturation_ceiling.equation: P_f^max = (2J_f + 1)/((2J_i + 1) + (2J_f + 1)): Gamma/4 for 3 ground + 1 excited, Gamma/3 for a Lambda system, Gamma/2 for a two-level atom
conv.saturation_ceiling.source: Berkeland Eqs. 13-14 and 21 (the special cases; the general form derived)

conv.saturation_intensity.corrected_form: gamma_hz fed in unconverted gives 8.09 mW/cm^2 (a 2 pi in every saturation parameter); Acton prints hbar for h; the random-orientation hbar omega^3 Gamma/(4 pi c^2) is exactly 3x the cycling value
conv.saturation_intensity.equation: I_sat = pi h c Gamma_partial/(3 lambda_vac^3) with Gamma_partial = 2 pi gamma_hz x branching ANGULAR; 171Yb+ 369.5 nm: 50.83 mW/cm^2

conv.scattering_channels.corrected_form: the absorption factor in an eliminated jump operator is this construction's own (Section 13's 'never both in a collapse operator' rule is for the explicit multi-level builder); the recoil quanta per photon eta_abs^2 + alpha eta_em^2 are the test
conv.scattering_channels.equation: one operator per (emitted polarization, direction node): Rayleigh diagonal over the resolved levels (Gamma_el/4 dissipator prefactor automatically), one Raman operator per (a, b), the out-of-manifold rates summed into the SINK at d > 2 and reported at d = 2; the absorbed beam's e^{+i k_b x} multiplies the emission kick; six axis directions about B with weights alpha_par/2 and alpha_perp/2 are exact in the first and second moments for every dipole pattern and every mode axis; rates scale with the played intensity as (Omega/Omega_nom)^p, p the Stark scaling power
conv.scattering_channels.symbol: L_{q', k_hat} = sqrt(w_k) sum_{a,b} r_{a->b q'} |b><a| (x) D(i(eta_abs - eta_em))

conv.scattering_channels_at_d_gt_2.corrected_form: an explicit scattering_channels=False is overridden rather than refused at d > 2, because a d > 2 register without leakage simulation carries a SINK level nothing can populate
conv.scattering_channels_at_d_gt_2.equation: run(..., internal_levels = d > 2) turns the flag on and records it in the run's notes; internal_levels = 2 keeps the d = 2 per-pulse estimate path of Section 4.3.2. The automatic switch turns on the register operators (leakage into the SINK, spin flips, the differential Rayleigh operator) WITHOUT the recoil displacements: Section 4.5.5's d > 2 requirement is about leakage, and the recoil-dressed operators (one per emission direction, per pulse, per branch) cost 30 to 50x more on the two-ion fixture, so they remain an explicit choice (scattering_channels=True with scattering_recoil='minimal' or 'vector'); a caller who set scattering_recoil='vector' keeps it
conv.scattering_channels_at_d_gt_2.symbol: internal_levels > 2 => SolverOptions.scattering_channels = True, scattering_recoil = 'off' unless 'vector' was asked for

conv.scattering_rate_object.corrected_form: the two-level Lorentzian saturates at Gamma/2 where the four-level manifold saturates at Gamma/4; a Gamma/6 prefactor with (2/3) s_o folds one polarization share too few
conv.scattering_rate_object.equation: one multi-level optical-Bloch steady state supplies the cooling rate W(Delta) in s^-1, the readout rates R_o, R_d, R_b and the dark-state physics; every photon rate is asserted against the equal-population ceiling n_e/(n_e + n_g) of the resonant closed manifold (Gamma/4 for the 171Yb+ F = 1 -> F' = 0 cycle); R_o is the rate of the CONDITIONAL bright state from the slow-manifold coarse graining, because the full steady state of a detected ion sits in F = 0 with weight R_d/(R_d + R_b) ~ 0.95
conv.scattering_rate_object.symbol: W(Delta) = sum_lines sum_k Tr(C_k^dag C_k rho_ss)

conv.section_9_9_convergence_regime.corrected_form: the run level carries the first arm (SolverOptions.convergence_check repeats the evolution at atol/10, rtol/10 and reports the change in the register populations as Diagnostics.convergence; off by default because it triples a run's cost), and hilbert.truncation.convergence_report runs all three arms of one case: tolerances/10, tolerances x10, and every resolved cap and the ENR excitation cap + 2 at unchanged tolerances (a mode whose growth would cross the dimension ceiling is left)
conv.section_9_9_convergence_regime.equation: Section 9.9: tightening tolerances by 10x (and, for the integrator ladder, loosening by 10x and comparing) and raising truncation caps by 2 changes reported probabilities by less than the stated test tolerance, for every validation case

conv.seed_keys.corrected_form: the shot slot is needed because photon counts are sampled per shot per ion; QuTiP's MultiTrajResult accumulates in completion order (4.4e-16 apart) and is not used for the average
conv.seed_keys.equation: one root SeedSequence per run spawned by (sample, trajectory, shot, ion, channel); a run over 1 and 18 workers agrees shot by shot and to 1e-12, because the engine averages trajectories in keyed order
conv.seed_keys.symbol: SeedSequence(root, spawn_key=(sample, trajectory, shot, ion, channel))

conv.servo_residual.corrected_form: sampling the raw quasi-static drift against a once-computed table would double-count the slow band a laboratory servos away
conv.servo_residual.equation: a Drift with a servo bandwidth is high-passed into its residual band over the shot clock: the residual variance of an OU drift of correlation time tau is sigma^2/(1 + 2 pi f_s tau) in the continuous limit and the drift's increment sigma^2 (2 dt/tau) for a lock re-armed every sample; the first sample carries no offset (the calibration measured it)
conv.servo_residual.symbol: x_k - x_hat_{k-1}, x_hat_k = x_hat_{k-1} + (1 - e^{-2 pi f_s dt})(x_k - x_hat_{k-1}), x_hat_0 = x_0

conv.shot_blocks_per_sample.corrected_form: not round-robin: one quasi-static draw per contiguous block of the shot clock is what the hardware does, and round-robin would give every sample the same mean shot time, so a drift over the sample times would produce no between-sample spread
conv.shot_blocks_per_sample.equation: shots are allocated in CONTIGUOUS BLOCKS, M_k = shots // S + 1 for the first shots % S samples, and sample k is drawn at the shot clock t0 + (sum_{j<k} M_j) T_rep; Diagnostics.shots_per_sample_realized reports the realized block sizes and Result.sample_of_shot the shot -> sample map Section 8.6 asks for
conv.shot_blocks_per_sample.symbol: sample k owns shots [sum_{j<k} M_j, sum_{j<=k} M_j)

conv.sideband_lineshape.corrected_form: Wineland's and Bluemel's Omega^2/(Omega^2 + delta^2/4) sin^2(t sqrt(Omega^2 + delta^2/4)) is the same curve at half the Omega: fitting it returns Omega/2 (a negative control), and it is never the fit function
conv.sideband_lineshape.equation: the calibration fit function: a carrier pi pulse at Omega t = pi, half depth (the Lorentzian weight 1/2) at delta = Omega; fitted with weighted least squares to the fine scan of every line

conv.sign_A_hfs_and_g_factors.corrected_form: A > 0 removes the clock points (no 43Ca+ point in 1 to 4000 G, no 9Be+ root in 8 to 16 mT), the ingest test of the sign
conv.sign_A_hfs_and_g_factors.equation: A_hfs is a signed input inferred from mu_I when not printed (9Be+, 43Ca+, 171Yb+ 3D[3/2]1/2 inverted); measured g_J replaces Lande; Steck's g_S = +2.0023193 (CODATA g_e is negative); nuclear Zeeman in Steck's form with a plus sign in H_B

conv.simultaneous_rb_units.corrected_form: the joint decay's (1 - p)(2^n - 1)/2^n is an error per layer of n Cliffords, never an error per Clifford beside a per-Clifford budget; two independent qubits at r_q = r_channel = 3.426e-4 reproduce the joint fit p = 0.999080 to 3.5 % in (1 - p), so the composition predicts the simultaneous decay; simultaneous RB runs on any number of ions
conv.simultaneous_rb_units.equation: simultaneous RB draws INDEPENDENT single-qubit Clifford sequences on several ions and plays them interleaved, so the group is the product C1 x ... x C1 and Section 13's n-qubit Clifford formula does not describe the joint decay. Every benchmarked qubit's own MARGINAL survival P(qubit q reads its target bit) is therefore fitted to A p_q^m + B and reported as r_q = (1 - p_q)/2 (RBResult.marginal_error_per_clifford), one Clifford on ONE qubit the unit -- the unit of the r that qubit measures alone and of the per-qubit composition budget.predicted['r_channel.q{i}'] = (Cliffords per sequence) x sum_kinds (pieces per Clifford) x (the kind's GATE_LOCAL channel reduced to THAT ONE qubit) -- and RBResult.error_per_clifford is their mean. The JOINT survival is fitted too and its (1 - p)(2^n - 1)/2^n kept as RBResult.joint_error_per_layer, the error per LAYER of n Cliffords, which equals sum_q r_q to first order (0.2 % at r_q = 2e-5, 3 % at 3.4e-4 over m up to 512) and is compared with r_channel_joint_layer, the same composition over one layer with the channels reduced to ALL benchmarked qubits
conv.simultaneous_rb_units.source: Gambetta et al., PRL 109, 240504 (2012); Magesan 2011; qutip_trap.benchmarks.rb
conv.simultaneous_rb_units.symbol: r_q = (1 - p_q)/2 per qubit; (1 - p)(2^n - 1)/2^n per layer

conv.solver_integrators.equation: the escalation ladder is dop853 then vern9; never a multistep method; atol 1e-10, rtol 1e-8

conv.solvers_read_the_device_modes.corrected_form: not wired: threading the table's beliefs into the surrogate and the resolved-mode selection would change what the full calibration converges to and which mode classes are selected
conv.solvers_read_the_device_modes.equation: Section 7.3's contract is that the solvers work at what the calibration table says, never at the device's hidden truth; every production caller builds GateModes from the device's crystal instead: gate_modes has a mode_frequencies_hz override no caller passes, CalibrationTable.lamb_dicke is written by the sideband experiment and read by no solver, and gate_modes has no eta override

conv.space_declaration_before_allocation.corrected_form: evaluating the guard after allocation forms an O(D)-non-zero identity first (64 MB at dimension 4194304; about 86 GB for the eight-ion eight-mode case), and an explicit JOINT_EXACT above the guards built a 37752-dimensional ENR space that took 20 GB and an hour before QobjEvo rejected its term
conv.space_declaration_before_allocation.equation: the guards of Section 11.5 are evaluated on the declared space before anything is allocated: HilbertSpace.check() asserts shape == prod(dims) arithmetically and forms the joint identity only below IDENTITY_CHECK_MAX_DIMENSION = 65536, so a HilbertSpace is a declaration (every operator on it lazy and cached), select_space evaluates within_budget on it (SpaceSelection.budget), and an explicit level='JOINT_EXACT' above the guards is refused with the dimension, the non-zeros and the two knobs named (joint_dimension_max, nnz_max)

conv.spin_motion_phases.corrected_form: Lee writes phi_S = -(half-sum); a '+phi' force axis would be a quarter-turn error
conv.spin_motion_phases.equation: phi_s = (phi_b + phi_r)/2, phi_m = (phi_b - phi_r)/2 of the two tone phases; the bichromatic force acts about phi_s + pi/2 in the same-Delta-k geometry (i eta(a + a^dag) carries an i), so MS(phi_0, phi_1, theta) sets phi_s,i = phi_i - pi/2 (qutip_trap.control.schedule)
conv.spin_motion_phases.source: Haljan 2005; Lee 2005 (opposite sign, converted at ingest)

conv.stark_compensation.corrected_form: an uncompensated -38 Hz light shift over the 100 us fixture gate costs about 1e-3 of fidelity (a 0.024 rad sigma_z rotation per ion); without the phase reference the compensated axis rotates by 2 pi delta_s t_start, so a compensated GPi2 one millisecond into a schedule loses 1.5e-2 = (2 pi 38 Hz 1 ms)^2/4 (anchor.m8.compensation_phase_reference)
conv.stark_compensation.equation: every tone of a scheduled pulse is detuned by the table's differential light shift for the played amplitude; both legs of a bichromatic segment move together (the motion phase is untouched); a correct belief keeps the pulse resonant with the shifted qubit, a wrong one leaves a reproducible detuning. The tones are phase-continuous in absolute time (the builder plays e^{-i(2 pi mu t - phi)}), so every compensated tone also carries the phase 2 pi delta_s(0) t_start (compensation_phase_rad) that references the compensation detuning to the qubit frame at the pulse start, minus, inside a multi-segment gate, the frame 2 pi int delta_s dt the earlier segments accumulated; the frame update after the pulse is 2 pi int delta_s dt (stark_phase_rad, frame_after)

conv.stark_scaling_with_amplitude.corrected_form: scaling every Stark entry as (Omega/Omega_cal)^2 turns the -0.1 Hz shift of a Raman waveform played at 550 times the derived carrier Rabi frequency into -70 kHz
conv.stark_scaling_with_amplitude.equation: p = 1 for a two-photon (Raman or light-shift) drive, whose Rabi frequency and differential Stark shift are both proportional to the intensity; p = 2 for a single-photon optical drive (Omega proportional to the field) and a microwave drive (the ac Zeeman shift proportional to B_1^2)

conv.static_error_primitive.corrected_form: Mount's R = exp[-(i/2) theta (1 + eps)(sigma_phi + delta Z)] and Cummins' quaternion pulse (axis (cos phi, sin phi, eps_d)/sqrt(1 + eps_d^2), angle theta sqrt(1 + eps_d^2)) identify eps_a = g and eps_d = f = delta/nu_1 with no rescaling on ingest
conv.static_error_primitive.equation: M = exp[-i theta {(1 + eps_a) rho(phi).sigma + eps_d sigma_z}/2], rho(phi) = (cos phi, sin phi, 0), exact for a square segment under time-independent errors; leading coefficients at theta = pi in 1 - F_K: primitive (pi^2/4) eps_a^2 and eps_d^2 exactly
conv.static_error_primitive.source: Kabytayev 2014 Sec. II A; Merrill and Brown; Cummins 2003; Mount 2015; qutip_trap.control.composite

conv.surface_electrode_geometry.corrected_form: not y0/h/d for one height, the rf Hessian angle as a mode axis, a maximum finder for the saddle, or sqrt(a(a + b)) with a as an unstated half-width
conv.surface_electrode_geometry.equation: widths from gap centre to gap centre; ion height h; the ion at the minimum of the total potential, not the rf null; escape point a saddle from f''(w) = 0; rf pseudopotential exactly isotropic transversely at a 2D null, axes set by the dc; five-wire h = sqrt(a(a + 2b))/2 for FULL widths; two-rail null x0 = ac/(b + c), y0 = sqrt(abc(a + b + c))/(b + c)

conv.terminal_measurement_event.equation: the terminal measure (the circuit's targets plus trailing measure operations) is the schedule's one event, after the last pulse and dead time, of the calibration table's detection window (the detector's when the table has none); a measure, reset or recool before a later gate is refused with a ScheduleError naming Section 8.5; the engine integrates to the end of the pulses, never through the detection window

conv.trajectory_count_two_phases.corrected_form: trajectory_target_tol defaults to None (the fixed ntraj with its keyed seed list) because QuTiP 5.3.1's target_tol accepts a zero-variance first batch (on a damped two-level system 26 trajectories at tol 0.1 and 604 at 0.02, but 2 at 0.005 and 0.001), and its firing point depends on scheduling, which the fixed-seed replay repairs
conv.trajectory_count_two_phases.equation: phase one runs mcsolve with target_tol on the population e_ops already assembled (SolverOptions.e_ops_for_target_tol gates it, SolverOptions.trajectory_target_tol sets the tolerance), under a SERIAL map so the firing point is reproducible, with ntraj as its cap and TARGET_TOL_MIN_TRAJECTORIES = 8 as its floor; phase two replays a keyed seed list of the estimated length
conv.trajectory_count_two_phases.symbol: target_tol -> n_est -> replay of n_est keyed seeds

conv.trajectory_grid_tau_c.corrected_form: an oversample of 4 gives dt = 0.785/omega_max, 7.9x coarser than the rule; the generator is the spectral method (valid for any tabulated S and validated by the periodogram), not an exact Ornstein-Uhlenbeck update
conv.trajectory_grid_tau_c.equation: the shortest correlation time a tabulated band carries is that of its fastest component, tau_c,min = 1/omega_max, so the rule reads dt <= 1/(10 omega_max); time_grid sets dt = pi/(omega_max x oversample), which meets it at oversample >= 10 pi = 31.4159

conv.two_photon_rabi.corrected_form: one symbol g means Omega/2 in two formulas and Omega in a third, inside two-photon formulas that differ by exactly that factor 2
conv.two_photon_rabi.equation: the code stores Omega (the hbar Omega/2 convention) and two ingest maps: g = Omega/2 for Monroe 1995, Wineland 1998, Ozeri and Section 4.5.5's g_{b,r} = E<d>/(2 hbar); g = Omega for the Lee comb chain (g_0 = gamma sqrt(I/2 I_sat)); Monroe's Omega = g_1 g_2/Delta is Omega_1 Omega_2/(2 Delta) in this convention

conv.validity_assertions.corrected_form: every guard takes an explicit escape keyword (allow_saturation, allow_unresolved, allow_strong_coupling, allow_fast_cooling, allow_invalid, allow_recoil_limited) for a source's own out-of-regime fixture: Marzoli's Fig. 3 (delta_aux = -Gamma_10), Morigi's EIT fixture (Omega_g 17 against gamma 20 MHz), Lechner's probe (Omega_pi/gamma = 0.29) and the 7/12 and 13/20 sideband-floor normalizations at Gamma/nu = 2
conv.validity_assertions.equation: the seven Section 4.2.8 (vii) conditions raise ValidityError at run time: assert_weak_drive on lorentzian_scattering_rate, stenholm_coefficients and eit_rate_coefficients (Omega/Gamma above 0.1, bloch.WEAK_DRIVE_MAX), assert_resolved_linewidth on sideband_floor (Gamma/nu above 0.1), assert_lamb_dicke on every level-A mode (eta^2 (2 nbar + 1) above 0.25), assert_adiabatic on every level-A mode (W above 0.1 nu or 0.1 min Gamma), EffectiveTwoLevel.assert_resolved (max(Gamma', gamma') above nu/5), assert_three_level_valid inside effective_two_level, and assert_doppler_recoil_limit inside doppler_cooling (Gamma <= omega_R = hbar k^2/2m)
conv.validity_assertions.symbol: eta^2(2n+1) << 1, Omega << Gamma, W << nu and << Gamma_min, Gamma' and gamma' << nu, Gamma > omega_R, s_aux << 1, |delta_aux| << Gamma_10 + Gamma_12

conv.virtual_z_propagation.corrected_form: IonQ's printed +theta holds in matrix order, not in time order
conv.virtual_z_propagation.equation: RZ(theta) shifts every later pulse phase phi -> phi - theta, gates read in time order: RZ(theta), GPi(0.5), GPi2(0) equals GPi(0.5 - theta), GPi2(-theta) followed by RZ(theta)

conv.wavelengths_vacuum.corrected_form: James's Fig. 4 quotes the calcium wavelengths in air (729.147 nm; vacuum 729.347 nm); an air value used as vacuum biases k by 274 ppm and gives the wrong laser frequency outright
conv.wavelengths_vacuum.equation: k = 2 pi/lambda_vac; every stored wavelength is a vacuum wavelength
conv.wavelengths_vacuum.source: James 1998; Roos 2000; NIST Sr II compilation

conv.worker_memory_cap.corrected_form: workers = None does not mean every CPU whatever the parent's size: forked from multi-gigabyte pytest parents, 18 workers exhausted memory; the 1-versus-N-worker identity of Section 9.9 is unaffected (the count is bookkeeping, and the reports state the count used)
conv.worker_memory_cap.equation: QuTiP's parallel map forks its workers, so each starts as a copy-on-write image of the parent and Python's reference counting dirties every page a worker touches: a parent of P bytes can turn N workers into up to N x P. worker_count returns min(requested or available_cpu_count, floor(MEMORY_FRACTION_FOR_WORKERS x physical memory / max(peak RSS, MIN_PARENT_BYTES))) with MEMORY_FRACTION_FOR_WORKERS = 0.5 and MIN_PARENT_BYTES = 512 MB: a 3 GB parent on a 48 GB machine gets 8 workers, a 6 GB one 4, a fresh process every CPU; the engine's mcsolve num_cpus and every map_tasks caller read worker_count, and EngineReport.workers and Diagnostics.workers state the count used
conv.worker_memory_cap.source: qutip_trap.dynamics.parallel (memory_worker_cap, worker_count); QuTiP 5.3.1 parallel map (the multiprocessing fork context)
conv.worker_memory_cap.symbol: workers <= floor(0.5 x physical memory / max(parent peak RSS, 512 MB))

conv.zero_point_energy.corrected_form: James keeps +hbar omega/2 per mode and uses the Kittel convention with a factor i and (a - a^dag), which the code never mixes in
conv.zero_point_energy.equation: H = sum hbar omega_k a^dag a, zero-point energy dropped; x = x0 (a + a^dag) with x0 = sqrt(hbar/(2 m omega))

published.crain_2019_snspd.corrected_form: 11 us is the AVERAGE detection time of the protocol, not the record window; the threshold optimum's window is 20 to 25 us (anchor.m5.crain_corrections_and_operating_point)
published.crain_2019_snspd.equation: 171Yb+ readout fidelity 99.931(6) % (1 - F = 6.9 x 10^-4) with the stop-on-first-photon protocol at 11 us average detection time; eps_sys = 4.356 %, 472 kcps detected bright rate, R_d = 341 Hz, R_b = 16.4 Hz, 4.2 cps background

published.harty_2014_epg.corrected_form: delta_eff = delta - delta_ac = +5.5 Hz during pulses; the identity timing is ambiguous in the paper (anchor.m2.harty_randomized_benchmarking)
published.harty_2014_epg.equation: measured error per computational gate 1.0(3) x 10^-6 by randomized benchmarking; the paper's own error model (12.1 us pi/2 pulses, 14 us dead time, +4.5 Hz detuning, 5e-4 pulse-area error) 0.81(14) x 10^-6
published.harty_2014_epg.source: Harty et al., PRL 113, 220501 (2014); arXiv:1403.1524, Fig. 7 and supplement

published.james_1998_axial_modes.corrected_form: the sign gauge of the eigenvectors is conv.mode_eigenvector_gauge, not James's
published.james_1998_axial_modes.equation: nu_p = sqrt(mu_p) nu_z with mu_1 = 1 (centre of mass) and mu_2 = 3 (stretch) for every N; mu_3 = 29/5 = 5.8 at N = 3, and 5.81, 5.818, 5.824, 5.829, 5.834, 5.838, 5.841 for N = 4..10

published.james_1998_positions.equation: u = -+ (1/2)^(2/3) = -+ 0.62996 for N = 2; -+ (5/4)^(1/3) = -+ 1.0772 and 0 for N = 3; Table 1 for N = 2..10 in units of the length scale l = (e^2/(4 pi eps0 m omega_z^2))^(1/3)
published.james_1998_positions.source: James, Appl. Phys. B 66, 181 (1998), Table 1 and Eqs. 3.2-3.4

published.kirchmair_2009_thermal_ms.corrected_form: F is dominated by the paper's technical terms (laser frequency noise 2e-3, heating Gamma_h t_g/2, a 1.4e-2 Rabi error), not by eta and nu (anchor.m4.kirchmair_ca40)
published.kirchmair_2009_thermal_ms.equation: Bell-state fidelity 0.993(1) at t_g = 50 us and 0.971(2) at 25 us with eta = 0.044 and nu/2pi = 1.232 MHz; parity contrast 0.964 on a thermal mode with nbar = 20(2)
published.kirchmair_2009_thermal_ms.source: Kirchmair et al., New J. Phys. 11, 023002 (2009)

published.monroe_1995_doppler.equation: 9Be+ Doppler-cooled occupations nbar = 0.47(5), 0.30, 0.18 at the 11.2, 18.2 and 29.8 MHz modes with Gamma/2pi = 19.4 MHz at Delta = -30 MHz; the paper's theoretical value for the 11.2 MHz mode 0.484

published.myerson_2008_readout.equation: threshold readout error eps = 1.8(1) x 10^-4 at n_c = 5.5 and t_b = 420 us; maximum-likelihood asymptote 0.87(11) x 10^-4; adaptive 1.0(1) x 10^-4 in 145 us on average

1.title: Purpose, scope and what "first principles" means here

1.1.text:
`qutip_trap` takes a quantum circuit and returns measurement results the way a trapped-ion quantum processor does, by simulating the physical process that produces them rather than by applying ideal gate matrices with an error model bolted on. The chain it reproduces:

1. A trap potential holds N ions of a chosen species; their equilibrium positions and collective motional modes follow from the trap parameters and the Coulomb interaction.
2. Laser cooling and optical pumping prepare the motional and internal states: a thermal (or near-ground) state per mode and a qubit state with a physical preparation error.
3. The circuit is compiled to the machine's native gates and then to a pulse schedule (which ions each pulse illuminates, with what Rabi-frequency envelope, detuning, phase and duration), every parameter taken from calibrations the simulator performs on the simulated device.
4. Each pulse evolves the joint state of qubits and motional modes under the spin-motion Hamiltonian, with heating, dephasing, photon scattering, addressing crosstalk and laser noise entering as physical channels whose rates follow from the device parameters.
5. Measurement is state-dependent fluorescence: photon counts over a detection window with leakage between the bright and dark manifolds, detector efficiency, background and neighbour crosstalk; a threshold or time-resolved discriminator turns counts into bits.
6. Results are returned per shot (bitstrings and optionally the photon-count records) and aggregated into counts and probabilities in the formats a cloud QPU returns.
1.1.title: Goal

1.2.text:
The simulator is exact at the level of a well-defined physical model and reports the three places where any simulation of this system approximates:

- **Model level.** Each ion is a small set of electronic levels (the qubit pair plus, where it matters, the leakage manifold), each motional mode a quantum harmonic oscillator, and light couples to them through the Hamiltonians of Part II. The optical rotating-wave approximation is taken everywhere (relative error Ω/ω_optical, below 10⁻⁸). Nothing else is dropped by default: the carrier, every sideband, the Debye-Waller factors, the off-resonant terms and the full time dependence of every pulse are kept, because the Hamiltonian is built from the exact displacement operator e^{iη(a+a†)} rather than from its Lamb-Dicke expansion. Raman drives add two approximations of comparable size, both reported with their magnitude: the adiabatic elimination of the far-detuned excited manifold, whose residual excited population is what the scattering channels use, and the replacement of the counter-rotating two-photon pairing at twice the qubit splitting by its second-order shift (Section 4.5.4). The Lamb-Dicke and sideband rotating-wave approximations are options, for speed and for reproducing textbook results, never defaults.
- **Truncation level.** Motional Fock spaces are truncated under the convergence policy of Section 5.5, and every run reports the population that reached the truncation boundary, so a result is either converged or flagged.
- **Size level.** The joint space of N ions and M modes has dimension 2^N Π_m d_m and becomes intractable beyond a few thousand: two or three ions with two or three resolved modes, or more ions with fewer resolved modes and frozen spectators (Sections 5.4, 11). Above that the GATE_LOCAL level (Section 5.4) simulates each pulse exactly on the ions it addresses and every mode they couple to, carries the motional state between gates by a tracked model, and reports the approximation it introduces; Section 9.8 validates it against the joint level where both are feasible.
1.2.title: What "exactly" can and cannot mean

1.3.text:
- Transport: shuttling, splitting, merging and junctions. The simulator models one crystal in one zone; it has no transport input, and transport dynamics and transport heating are out of scope.
- Photonic interconnects, and quantum error correction logic (the simulator runs circuits; a QEC stack is a client of `run`).
- Compilation optimality: the compiler is correct and produces the native gate set through verified templates (Section 7.7), an arbitrary two-qubit unitary at three entangling gates; gate-count optimization beyond the standard identities is a client concern.
- Mid-circuit measurement: `measure`, `reset` and `recool` are IR operations and a `Schedule` carries their positions, but the scheduler refuses one that precedes a later gate, because the detection back-action of Section 8.5 is not modelled.
- Crystal melting: background-gas collisions are instantaneous events with an outcome distribution (heating kick, reorder, loss, dark ion; Section 6.7), heralded per shot; after a loss or dark-ion event the remaining ions stay on the nominal crystal, which the diagnostics state.
- Planar crystals: a linear chain is required (the crystal solver raises `ZigzagError` beyond the zigzag threshold), and the multi-ion rf (Floquet) frame is not built, so every multi-ion result is in the pseudopotential frame (Sections 4.1.1, 4.1.7).
- Mixed-species dynamics: the crystal layer computes mixed-species positions, modes and per-species Lamb-Dicke parameters (Section 4.1.7) and sympathetic cooling is modelled at the rate level (Section 4.2.5), but no gate on a mixed crystal is scheduled or validated.
- Recalibration in the loop: drift enters through the dynamical samples at the shot clock and an optional servo (Section 7.5), not through repeated calibration.
1.3.title: Non-goals

1.4.text: The user writes or imports a circuit, picks a machine (a device model: species, ion count, trap, beam geometry, noise, detector) and asks for results. The public surface is a `Machine` (a `Device`, the roles its beams play, the calibration table and the option objects `Physics`, `Numerics` and `Readout`) with `run`, `submit` (the same run in a worker process behind a `Job`), `compile`, `schedule`, `engine`, `calibrated`, `estimate`, `error_model` and `hash`; a circuit IR (`Circuit`) with the native gates (GPi, GPi2, MS with two phases and an angle, ZZ, virtual RZ) and a compiler from standard gates; importers for OpenQASM 2 and the IonQ circuit JSON and exporters to IonQ's result formats; a Qiskit `BackendV2`; the laboratory of simulated experiments (Rabi, Ramsey, sideband spectroscopy, thermometry, heating rate, MS and parity scans) that calibration uses and users call to reproduce laboratory measurements; and the benchmarks (randomized benchmarking, GHZ fidelity, quantum volume), each with the simulator's own error budget beside it. The methods of `Machine` walk down the five levels the application shows (Section 14.2): the machine (`run`), the circuit (`compile`), the schedule (`schedule`), the dynamics (`engine`) and the physics (the `Device`). The application (Section 14) uses only this public API.
1.4.title: Users and interfaces

1.5.text: Python 3.13 (pinned by mise), `uv` for environments and dependencies, QuTiP 5.3.x as the simulation engine (5.3.1 with NumPy 2.5 and SciPy 1.18), NumPy and SciPy as the numerical base. Coefficients are NumPy arrays and Python functions, so Cython is optional; no other simulation framework is used; matplotlib is an optional extra. The application uses Flet (flet.dev), which renders through Flutter: one code base gives a desktop window, a browser UI served from the host process, or packaged bundles, with `flet-charts` for the plots. Flet is an optional extra, so the core has no UI dependency. Event handlers may be async and the page offers `run_task` and `run_thread`, so simulations run in worker processes and post progress through the page's pubsub. Flet's static web build runs Python in the browser through Pyodide, three to five times slower than native and without processes: it is the GitHub Pages site, with QuTiP compiled for Pyodide by the Pages workflow (no WebAssembly wheel exists on PyPI) and the app's worker running in-process.
1.5.title: Constraints inherited from the environment

11.1.text:
Reference machine: QuTiP 5.3.1, NumPy 2.5, SciPy 1.18, Python 3.13, Apple Accelerate BLAS, 18 CPUs. Fixture: two 171Yb+ ions at ω_x, ω_y, ω_z = 3.0, 2.9, 1.0 MHz with the Raman Δk in the transverse plane at 30° from x (modes x-COM 3.000, x-rocking 2.828 and y-COM 2.900 MHz with η = 0.080, ±0.0824 and 0.047), a bichromatic Mølmer-Sørensen pulse at ε/2π = 10 kHz and the maximally entangling closure ηΩ/ε = 1/2 (a 100 µs single loop), the exact drive operator of Section 5.1.1, `sesolve` at atol 10⁻¹⁰ and rtol 10⁻⁸ from |↓↓⟩|0…0⟩, d_m Fock levels per mode. Times are per 100 µs gate **[recomputed here]**:

| Joint dimension | Assembled, merged dense | Assembled, merged CSR | Factorized kernel | Factorized kernel, rotating frame (default) | Evaluations per 20 µs, Schrödinger picture |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 48 (1 mode, d_m = 12) | 0.15 s | 0.1 s | 1.6 s | 0.7 s | 1.9 × 10⁴ |
| 256 (2 modes, d_m = 8) | 0.6 s | 1.7 s | 2.5 s | 0.8 s | 2.1 × 10⁴ |
| 864 (3 modes, d_m = 6) | 6 s | 25 s | 4.9 s | 1.2 s | 2.4 × 10⁴ |
| 2048 (3 modes, d_m = 8) | 2.1 min | 3.6 min | 12 s | 1.9 s | 3.5 to 3.8 × 10⁴ |

`dop853` is 10 to 25% faster than `vern9` on all but one row, and the two integrators' final states agree to 1.3 × 10⁻⁷ (dimension 48) to 5.8 × 10⁻⁷ (2048) in norm, which is what "identical results" means in this specification; the two constructions of one operator agree to 10⁻¹³ to 2 × 10⁻⁸. Of the assembled forms the merged dense operator is fastest at every measured size: for two ions Σ_i(σ₊^i D_i + h.c.) fills half the matrix, where a CSR product (0.5 to 0.6 ns per non-zero, memory-bound) loses to the dense BLAS product (0.16 ns per element at dimension 2048). The engine's `auto` kernel assembles the small spaces and factorizes the large ones; `mesolve` always uses CSR, because there the Liouvillian's memory decides. The rotating frame (Section 11.3 item 10) cuts the right-hand-side evaluations 3.2, 4.1, 5.0 and 7.7 times on these rows. The real 100 µs pulse of the two-ion example device on the space [2, 2, 9, 15] that the cap rule selects takes 5.1 s in the Schrödinger picture and 1.0 s in the rotating frame (43 against 7 integrator steps per period of the 3 MHz mode). Density-matrix evolution stops being practical near dimension 300 (a 10⁵ × 10⁵ Liouvillian), so dissipation at scale runs on trajectories.

On the two-ion example machine (`presets.yb171_chain(2)`): the surrogate calibration takes about 6 s; a Bell circuit with 2000 shots about 3.5 s (five carrier pulses and one entangling gate on the space [2, 2, 11, 13]); a 384-Clifford single-qubit RB sequence 2 s (its carrier pulses run on the internal space through the propagator cache); a two-qubit Clifford about 10 s; the Bell circuit at `level="GATE_LOCAL"` about 5 s (17 s on the reference tomography route); a two-qubit quantum-volume circuit about a minute; calibration by simulated experiments about twelve minutes. The three-ion GHZ circuit at dimension 1152 takes several minutes per run. Randomized benchmarking to the 10⁻⁵ level therefore runs hundreds of single-qubit Cliffords and thousands of shots, while two-qubit RB and quantum volume run at tens of Cliffords and a handful of circuits, and their results say so.
11.1.title: Measured cost

11.2.text:
Wall time is the number of right-hand-side evaluations times the cost of one application of H(t) to the state.

- **Evaluations.** 1.9 × 10⁴ to 3.8 × 10⁴ per 20 µs with `dop853` in the Schrödinger picture (27 to 52 steps per period of the 3 MHz mode at 12 evaluations per step, growing with the cap), 1.2 times more with `vern9`: a 100 µs pulse needs 1 to 2 × 10⁵ evaluations and a 10 µs single-qubit pulse 1 to 2 × 10⁴, and the rotating frame divides both by 3 to 8.
- **Cost per evaluation.** Dominated by the drive operator: σ₊^i ⊗ Π_m D_m has 2^{N−1} Π_m d_m² non-zeros per ion, and the merged Σ_i(σ₊^i D_i + h.c.) has N 2^N Π_m d_m², a fraction N/2^N of the (2^N Π_m d_m)² matrix, shared by the tones through the coefficient. A CSR product costs 0.5 to 0.6 ns per non-zero (memory-bound at about 35 GB/s, 20 bytes per non-zero); a dense product 0.16 ns per element beyond cache and 0.07 to 0.09 ns inside it. At dimension 2048 that is 1.2 ms per evaluation in CSR and 0.65 ms dense, and 3.0 ms for four unmerged dense terms.
- **Scaling.** Cost = a + b × (elements touched per evaluation) × evaluations with a ≈ 0.02 s and b = 0.16 ns (dense beyond cache) or 0.58 ns (CSR) predicts every measured row within about 20% (`Machine.estimate` uses it). Doubling d_m on three modes multiplies the elements by 64 and the evaluations by about 1.4; a fourth mode at d_m = 8 multiplies the elements by 64; an extra ion multiplies the dense cost by 4 and the CSR cost by 2(N + 1)/N. Four ions with three modes at d_m = 8 (dimension 8192; 6.7 × 10⁷ dense elements, 1.1 GB, or 1.7 × 10⁷ non-zeros) cost about 10 ms per evaluation assembled, 25 to 30 minutes per 100 µs gate, which the factorized kernel (24 against 512 amplitudes per mode product) brings back to minutes. Eight ions with eight axial modes at N_exc = 6 have a drive operator of 1.15 × 10⁹ non-zeros (18.5 GB per ion), which is why the reductions below are not optional and why the JOINT_EXACT range of Section 5.4 is a dimension budget.
11.2.title: Cost model

11.3.text:
1. **ENR truncation** (option) for a group of cold, undriven modes carried dynamically: C(M + N_exc, N_exc) states instead of Π_m d_m, with the exponential of the ENR sum generator as the operator (Section 5.1.1). An ENR group is not a product space, so item 4 does not apply to it and the two are never composed on the same modes.
2. **Mode selection per pulse.** A mode leaves a pulse's resolved set when its closed-form residual displacement and entangling-angle contribution (Section 4.4.3 integrals over the pulse's actual detuning schedule) are both negligible, |α_m(τ)|²(2n̄_m + 1) < 10⁻⁶ and |χ_m(τ)| < 10⁻⁴ by default, never on η alone: a mode with η = 10⁻³ two kilohertz from a tone contributes more than one with η = 0.05 a megahertz away. A mode above this pair but with |χ_m| below the freeze tolerance (0.05 rad) is frozen rather than dropped. Dropped modes evolve freely (their heating still applies) and the summed dropped contribution is reported.
3. **Frozen spectators** (Section 5.2): modes far from every tone leave the joint space and enter through per-shot Debye-Waller factors, with the off-resonant excitation bound reported.
4. **Mode-factorized application of the drive operator** (product spaces only). Because Π_m D_m is a tensor product, applying it mode by mode costs Σ_m d_m multiply-adds per amplitude instead of Π_m d_m (24 against 512 for three modes at d_m = 8), through a matrix-free right-hand side registered as a QuTiP data-layer type, exact to round-off. The measured gain is smaller than that ratio because each factor step has a fixed cost (about 2.5 µs per step plus 0.6 ns per multiply-add, against 0.57 ns per non-zero assembled), so the `auto` kernel follows the measured crossover: assembled below dimension 440, factorized above (299 against 24 µs per evaluation at 2048). An ENR group and every `mesolve` segment stay assembled.
5. **Cached operators.** The σ₊ ⊗ D_i matrices (or their factors) per (ion, Δk, space) are built once. Pulse propagators are reused only on internal-state-only spaces (Section 5.3), never on the joint space; there the cached propagator is the step's channel and the GATE_LOCAL tomography reads its Kraus operator off it, while on a joint space the tomography propagates the Π_i d_i internal basis columns, never the D × D propagator. One engine serves a whole GATE_LOCAL walk, and the one-ion idle channels are cached by (ion, duration, engine setup, sample, options).
6. **Interaction frame for slow pulses** (option): for microwave or co-propagating Raman single-qubit gates with negligible motional coupling, the motion factors out and the pulse evolves on the internal space alone with the exact Debye-Waller reduction folded into Ω.
7. **Sideband-truncated interaction picture** (Section 5.2), when the cap is large and few sidebands matter.
8. **GATE_LOCAL** (Section 5.4) above the joint-exact range.
9. **Trajectories and parallelism.** Trajectories, branches and quasi-static samples are spread over the cores with QuTiP's parallel `map`, which forks and pickles, so every `QobjEvo` coefficient is a module-level named function, a `Coefficient` or an array: a lambda or closure raises `PicklingError` under `map="parallel"` on 5.3.1 (only `map="loky"`, an optional dependency, survives it), and the builder never emits closures **[corrected]**.
10. **Exact rotating frame** (`SolverOptions.rotating_frame`, default on). Every ket segment integrates iφ̇ = Θ†V(t)Θφ with Θ = e^{−iH₀t} for the diagonal H₀ = H_mot + H_int (plus a constant Stark shift): the phases are applied around the unchanged drive operators of items 4 and 5, collapse operators that are eigenoperators of ad_{H₀} carry e^{iλt}, and expectation values, stored and final states are phased back. A segment with a collapse operator that is not an eigenoperator (a recoil kick, the intensity-noise channel) stays in the Schrödinger picture, because `mcsolve` forms c†c from the operators it is given. Nothing is expanded or truncated: results equal the Schrödinger-picture integration to the solver tolerance, and `SegmentReport.frame` names the picture each segment used **[recomputed here]**.
11.3.title: Reduction techniques, in the order they are applied

11.4.text: The budgets of Section 14.7 follow from Section 11.1. Re-simulating one trajectory of a zoomed 100 µs entangling pulse with its recorded noise sample takes under a second up to about dimension 864 and about 2 s at 2048 in the rotating frame; anything that needs an ensemble (a representative jump record, a process matrix from 16 tomography inputs) and recalibration by simulated experiment run as background jobs with progress, the record's stored traces shown at once and stale badges until they finish. The re-derivation of modes, η, pulse-solver solutions and closed-form channel estimates after a device change is immediate, with pulse re-solves of at most about 10 s per pair in the background. App-side channel replay of a 20-qubit, 100-gate circuit takes seconds.
11.4.title: Interactive budgets for the application

11.5.text: States are dense complex128; at dimension 10⁶ a state is 16 MB, and a trajectory ensemble is stored only as final states or sampled observables. An assembled drive operator at dimension 2048 (2.1 × 10⁶ non-zeros) is about 40 MB in CSR and 67 MB dense and grows as Π_m d_m²; the factorized kernel stores only the per-mode D_m. The level policy refuses to build a joint space above `joint_dimension_max` (default 4096, from the cost model of Section 11.2) or a drive operator above `nnz_max` non-zeros (default 2 × 10⁷, estimated from Π_m d_m² and the ion count) and routes `level="auto"` to GATE_LOCAL; an explicit `level="JOINT_EXACT"` above either guard is refused, and a cap that would grow past a guard during a run is refused the same way. Parallel maps fork their workers, each a copy-on-write image of the caller that can grow toward its size, so `SolverOptions.workers = None` caps the count to keep the workers' worst-case total (each as large as the parent's peak resident size) within half of physical memory; an explicit request is capped the same way, `QUTIP_TRAP_MAX_WORKERS` caps the default count only, a count of one runs in-process on the serial map, and `Diagnostics.workers` and `Diagnostics.map` report what ran.
11.5.title: Memory

12.text:
- **Anomalous heating has no first-principles model.** The heating rate follows exactly from the electric-field noise spectral density S_E(ω) **[verified]**, but S_E is empirical: measured values span ten orders of magnitude, the distance exponent is disputed (2.6 to 4.0) and no microscopic mechanism is established **[verified]**. S_E(ω) is therefore a device input (constant, power law or tabulated) with its provenance, and every heating number is apparatus-local.
- **Noise enters as spectra the sources do not supply.** Electric-field, magnetic-field, laser-phase and intensity noise are device spectra with declared white parts; the sources give exponents and single numbers (α_S = 0.8(1), no spatial correlation length, no mechanism for the 1.2× and 1.35× excess over the uniform-field model at 15 and 25 ions, and the King and Rohde measurements disagree on whether the non-centre-of-mass modes heat, which the correlation-length input decides), so the absolute infidelities of the filter-function layer (Section 6.9) are conditional on the device's spectra. No source bounds non-Gaussian, non-stationary or quantum-bath noise; the filter functions assume zero-mean Gaussian wide-sense-stationary classical noise, and no source supplies an infrared regulator, so ω_min is an input reported beside χ (Section 6.9).
- **Published fidelities are not reproducible from first principles.** No mode-participation matrix and no AM or FM segment amplitudes are published for any chain whose fidelities are quoted, so Section 9 treats such reproductions as consistency anchors with stated assumptions.
- **The ZZ native gate has no published physical model**; the MS gate dressed by two single-qubit rotations is inferred from the 220 µs duration difference, implemented as that construction and labelled inferred (Section 4.4.4).
- **Composite pulses and decoupling.** PD6's phase vector at arbitrary angle needs numerical continuation rather than a printed formula; Low-Yoder-Chuang's AP3 and NS2 closed forms and prefactors were not transcribed, so same-order sequences are ranked by order, not by prefactor; no source gives a rule for choosing a family from a measured error triple, a scheduler objective, a second-order filter function, a closed-form detuning filter function, a multiplicative amplitude-noise filter function, multi-axis decoupling or an implementable dynamically corrected gate. The direct-RB error-rate prefactor is undecidable from the published data ((15/16)(1 − p) and 1 − p both fit), and is recorded as an open convention (Section 7.9).
- **The Bermudez three-variant mapping of ε onto Pauli channels** is named by the sources but specified by none with equations, so it is omitted; the Pauli twirl and the depolarizing rate of Section 6.8 are provided.
- **Comb drives.** The comb literature supplies no spontaneous-emission rate, no multi-ion multi-mode construction, no wave-front tolerance that closes, no beat-note or repetition-rate noise spectra, no fourth-order shift for a resonant carrier drive, and one species at one wavelength (171Yb+ at 355 nm); the crossover between the ultrafast-kick and resolved-sideband pictures is unbounded, the fourth-order Stark series is marginal at the quoted full power (Ω₀ above the detuning it expands in), and the factor 2 between the two internally consistent intensity-to-Rabi chains is contested (Section 4.3.7).
- **Readout apparatus quantities** (detection efficiency, background, a D-manifold branching fraction the sources do not tabulate for 171Yb+) are presets, never species constants; no hyperfine-resolved coherent-population-trapping Liouvillian and a dark-resonance map for 88Sr+ only are published (Section 8.1).
- **Cetina's quasi-static amplitude model is validated only for n̄ ≫ 1**; sideband-cooled modes should show revivals no source characterizes, and the exact position-operator implementation (Section 6.2) is compared with the closed forms only where they apply.
- **Micromotion beyond first order in q**, the rf phase relative to the pulse envelope, beam-intensity and pointing spectra and the laser linewidth as a spectrum are absent from the sources; the Floquet treatment of Section 4.1.1 covers the first, and the drive coefficients take the rest as supplied spectra. The quantized multi-ion Floquet frame is absent from the sources and Landa's classical coupled-mode construction is not built, so every N > 1 result is in the pseudopotential frame with C₀ per axis.
- **Unvalidated couplings.** The photon-recoil kernel of Section 4.2.8 is untested as the recoil operator of the Raman and Rayleigh dissipators (Section 4.5.5), and the E2 ac Stark shift of Section 4.5.7 has no published number to validate it.
- **Fock truncation for the exact exponential Hamiltonian at large n̄ has no sourced criterion**; the convergence policy of Section 5.5 is standard practice, enforced by the paired-cutoff test.
- **Implementation limits, stated where they arise:** rf phase-noise sideband heating and 2ω_sec parametric heating are not in a run's noise model, and the differential dc mode drift is drawn as independent per-mode offsets (Section 6.2); the played chain converts Raman and optical drives only, so a miscalibrated table leaves microwave, light-shift and gradient drives error-free, and the table's fitted η is read by no solver (Section 7.3); the 171Yb+ 935 nm repump cycle cannot close without the untabulated 297 nm branch (Section 8.1); mid-circuit measurement is refused (Section 8.5).
- **Transport**, **planar crystals**, **mixed-species gates** and **recalibration in the loop** are out of scope (Section 1.3).
12.title: Open physics and inputs the sources do not supply

13.text:
Every quantity below has at least two conventions in the primary literature, and published factor-of-2 (and 2π, and √N) errors trace to mixing them. The simulator adopts one convention per quantity and names the source it follows; the third column also names the forms in the sources that must not be imported as they stand. Modules restate the row they implement, and tests pin the conversions. The `conv.*` records of the provenance ledger are the machine-readable form of these rows.

| Quantity | Convention | Follows; forms not to import |
|---|---|---|
| Frequencies | internal frequencies angular (rad/s); every public number an ordinary frequency in Hz (`units.Hz`), converted once with an explicit 2π (`rad_s_from_hz`, `hz_from_rad_s`); internal names carry the unit (`_hz`, `_rad_s`, `_per_s`); a linewidth `gamma_hz` is the upper level's total decay rate over 2π | RMP 2003 (which writes ν for an angular frequency). Not: "γ = 2π × 19.6 MHz", "γ/2π = 60 MHz" and "19.7 MHz" used interchangeably; Leung's 3.045 MHz read as rad/s |
| Names of public numbers | every public float carries its unit suffix (`_hz`, `_s`, `_m`, `_w`, `_gauss`, `_rad`, `_v`, `_pa`, `_cps`; `_turns` only at the IonQ boundary); error-model names: `p_*` a probability per operation, `*_rate` per second, `*_ratio` a fraction of another probability, `*_scale` a dimensionless multiplier | this package |
| Logarithms | natural | Burrell 2010. Not: Harty's Fig. 3 log₁₀ |
| Mathieu equation | d²x/dξ² + [a − 2q cos 2ξ]x = 0, ξ = ω_rf t/2, a = 4Z∣e∣Uα/(mω_rf²), q = 2Z∣e∣Ũα′/(mω_rf²); the Mathieu q and the charge Q are distinct names (`q_mathieu`, `Q_charge`) | Leibfried et al. 2003. Not: Wineland 1998's and Berkeland 1998's +2q cos (a half-period shift); House 2008's Q = −q with its Eq. 7 matrix of the wrong sign (a stable trap reads unstable) |
| Characteristic exponent | the monodromy matrix, β on the principal branch (−1, 1], ω_j = β_jΩ/2; β ≈ √(a + q²/2) only as a check | Floquet theory. Not: RMP Eqs. 10-11 (index error) |
| Floquet function and rf phase origin | the adopted sign fixes the origin: u(t) ≈ e^{iνt}[1 − (q/2)cos ω_rf t]/(1 − q/2), c_{±1}/c₀ = −q/((2 ± β)² − a) | Section 4.1.1. Not: the RMP's quantum section and Wineland's [1 + (q/2)cos], the same physics half an rf period later |
| Micromotion factors | η_eff = ηC₀ with the Wronskian-normalized C₀ of Section 4.1.1, applied once, in `Crystal.lamb_dicke`; excess micromotion as the phase modulation J_n(β) on every drive (gates, cooling, detection) | Section 4.1.1; Wineland Eqs. 71-72; Berkeland Eq. 21 (misprint corrected). Not: the RMP's (1 + q/2)⁻¹; J_n applied to gates only |
| Coupled Floquet normalization | companion matrix F = [[0, 𝟙], [−(A + 2Q cos 2τ), 0]], U(0) = 𝟙, monodromy at τ = π; Vᵗ(0)U(0) = i/2 elementwise; Γ⁻¹ by the closed form, never a dagger | Landa 2012. Not: House's sign; the paper-literal inverted C₋₂ step |
| rf amplitude and pseudopotential | V_rf the peak of a cos(Ω_rf t) drive; ψ = Q²∣E∣²/(4mΩ²) in joules; Chiaverini's and Madsen's V₀ are differential amplitudes (±V₀/2), Home's Φ a pseudopotential in volts, Kielpinski's φ an energy | House; Wesenberg. Not: an rms reading (doubles the depth, √2 on every rf frequency) or a peak-to-peak one (quarters the depth); the charge applied twice |
| Surface-electrode geometry | widths from gap centre to gap centre; ion height h; the ion at the minimum of the total potential, not the rf null; the escape point a saddle from G′(Z) = 0; the rf pseudopotential isotropic transversely at a 2D null, so the dc sets the axes | House; Wesenberg; Nizamani. Not: the rf Hessian angle as a mode axis; a maximum finder for the saddle; Nizamani's q_N in ω = qΩ/(2√2) |
| Ladder operators | x̂ = x₀(a + a†), x₀ = √(ħ/2mω) | RMP Eq. 26. Not: Brownnutt arXiv v1's √(ħmω); the factor 4 under the root in Ozeri 2007 and Baldwin 2021 |
| Zero-point energy | dropped, H = Σħω_k a†a | Wineland 1998; Marquet 2003 (James keeps ħω/2, a convention) |
| Mode index | every mode index is a position in `Crystal.modes`, ordered axial, transverse_1, transverse_2, ascending in frequency within a family; eigenvectors unit norm, last component positive | Section 4.1.3. Not: eigensolver order; James's transverse numbering by decreasing frequency |
| Mass-weighted eigenvectors and parity | orthonormal in u_i = √m_i z_i only (physical amplitudes carry 1/√m_i); the overall sign a gauge, relative signs physical; inversion parity p = +1 is an antisymmetric displacement pattern, exempt from uniform-field noise and uncoolable by a centre ion | Morigi-Walther; Kielpinski; Wübbena; Home. Not: renormalizing raw displacements (20 to 160% off at μ ≠ 1); Morigi-Walther Eq. 9's oblique form; "even" read as "in-phase" |
| Lamb-Dicke parameter | η_{i,m} = (Δk·ê_m) c_{i,m} √(ħ/(2m_i ω_m)) with the ion's own mass and the mass-weighted unit-norm eigenvector component, the participation counted once (Section 4.1.7) | Wineland 1998 Eq. 33; Monroe 2020; Home 2013 Eq. 19; Morigi-Walther Eq. 12. Not: the per-ion COM η of Sørensen-Mølmer and Leung, which contains 1/√N; Lee's 1/√2 inside η; Ozeri's z₀ = √(ħ/4Mω) (Srinivas's r₀ with the total mass belongs to the gradient force, Section 4.4.5) |
| Heating rate | a quoted rate is d⟨n⟩/dt at n = 0, Γ_h = ΓN̄; thermal diffusion Γ(2N̄ + 1); collapse operators √(Γ(N̄ + 1)) a and √(ΓN̄) a†; ṅ ∝ ω^{−(α+1)} when S_E ∝ ω^{−α} | Brownnutt 2015 Eqs. 15-17; Wineland Eq. 62 (typo fixed). Not: the journal's 2aρ†a†; the equal-rate pair {√ṅ a, √ṅ a†} with a finite N̄ (it is the N̄ ≫ 1 limit) |
| Electric-field noise density | single-sided S_E, Γ_h = e²S_E/(4mħω), converted at ingest to the noise layer's two-sided angular spectra | Brownnutt Eqs. 11-12. Not: the two-sided e²S_E/(2mħω) unconverted; the arXiv Turchette Eq. 3 (the PRA is consistent) |
| Noise spectra | every stored spectrum two-sided in angular frequency with the e^{−iωt} kernel and a separately declared white level (Section 6.1) | Section 6.1 |
| Motional dephasing operator | L = a†a √(2/τ); the coherence of ∣n⟩ + ∣n′⟩ decays at (n − n′)²/τ | Ballance 2016 |
| Qubit dephasing operator | L = √(γ_φ/2) σ_z, so the coherence decays at γ_φ and γ_φ = 1/T₂ for the white part; a measured T₂ is split into its quasi-static (Gaussian) and white (exponential) parts before use | Section 6.3. Not: conventions giving 2/T₂ |
| Debye-Waller statistics | shot to shot: Ω constant within a shot and distributed across shots; never the ensemble-mean factor inside one shot | Wineland 1998; Cetina 2022 |
| Rabi frequency | H = (ħΩ/2)σ₊e^{…} + h.c., carrier π pulse at Ωt = π; the π time is convention independent, so what breaks is any formula written in the symbol | RMP 2003; Monroe 2020; Lee 2005. Not: P = sin²(Ωt) (Wineland 1998, Monroe 1995, Blümel 2021 Eq. S28), Uys's Ω_R = μE₀/(2ħ) and Wineland's stretched-element g with Ωτ_π = π/2, each half this Ω; Joshi's Ω referenced to the S₁/₂-P₃/₂ stretched line (√(3/2) in Ω, 3/2 in s on the D1 σ line) |
| Single-photon coupling g | not a stored symbol: the code stores Ω, with ingest maps g = Ω/2 (Monroe 1995, Wineland 1998, Ozeri, Section 4.5.5) and g = Ω (the Lee comb chain, Section 4.3.7); Monroe's Ω = g₁g₂/Δ is Ω₁Ω₂/(2Δ) | Sections 4.2.2, 4.3.7, 4.5.5 |
| Two-photon Rabi frequency | Ω_R = Σ_e Ω₂*Ω₁/(2Δ_e) with the single-photon Ω_j = E_j⟨e∣d·ε̂_j∣g⟩/ħ in the ħΩ/2 convention and Δ_e = ω_L − ω_eg; light shift δ_g = Σ∣Ω∣²/(4Δ_e) (Section 4.5.4) | Wineland 2003 Eqs. 2.3, 2.10 (his overall minus sign is a phase convention). Not: RMP A13 and Wineland 2003 read as Ω₁Ω₂/Δ_R, 2× too large |
| Rabi frequency from intensity | Ω = E₀∣ε_q⟨F′ m_F + q∣d_q∣F m_F⟩∣/ħ with E₀ = √(2I/(ε₀c)); on the cycling transition Ω = Γ√(I/(2I_sat)), and s = I/I_sat = 2Ω²/Γ² there only | Steck. Not: Noek's s in the (Γ/6, 2/3) detection form, which is I/(3I_sat) |
| Saturation intensity | I_sat = πhcΓ/(3λ³) with Γ the angular partial rate of the cycling branch, Γ_partial = 2π γ_hz × branching (Section 4.5.2) | Steck. Not: Acton's ħ for h; `gamma_hz` unconverted |
| Saturation parameters | s₀ = I/I_sat per beam on resonance (Ejtemaee) and s = (Ω²/2)/(Γ²/4 + Δ²) per beam, detuning-suppressed and normalized on the S₁/₂-P₃/₂ stretched line (Joshi), namespaced and never aliased; s_Joshi = (3/2)s₀(Γ/2)²/((Γ/2)² + Δ²) **[background]** | Ejtemaee-Haljan 2017; Joshi 2020 |
| Detuning | δ = ω_drive − ω_transition, red negative; μ the beat-note detuning from the carrier; δ_{i,m} = μ_i − ω_m always two-indexed; the composite-pulse detuning error δ̂ = ε_d = Δ/Ω (Kabytayev and Cummins's ε_d = f = δ/ν₁) | RMP 2003. Not: Landsman's δ measured from a mode; Mount's dimensionless δ; Sørensen-Mølmer's ε = ν − δ from the sideband |
| Itano-Wineland detuning | their (ω₀ − ω) is positive for red: the sign flips on import and the recoil shift is added | Itano-Wineland 1982 Eqs. 16-29 |
| EIT detuning | Δ > 0 and Ω_r² = 4ν(ν + Δ) in the adopted sign, Ω_r = √(Ω₁² + Ω₂²) | Section 4.2.3. Not: Morigi's Δ, the negative of this one (her optimum 4ν(ν − Δ)) |
| Effective wavevector | Δk = k₁ − k₂ with beam 1 coupling to the upper level, ∣Δk∣ = 2k sin(θ_cross/2) from the configured geometry; k for one beam, 0 for a microwave | RMP; Wineland 1998; Lee 2005. Not: Landsman's k₂ − k₁; Lee's arXiv v1 Eq. 2 (the journal version is right) |
| Optical phase on σ₊ | e^{+i(Δk·X̄_i − Δφ_i)}; beam-path and ion-position drift one scalar per ion per pulse | Monroe 2020 Eqs. 16, 18. Not: the e^{−i(…)} of Monroe Eqs. 3, 5 and Lee Eqs. 3, 5 |
| Polarization components | ε̂ = Σ_q ε_q ê_q in the spherical basis about B, ê_{±1} = ∓(x̂ ± iŷ)/√2, ê₀ = ẑ; helicity q_γ = +1 (σ⁺), 0 (π), −1 (σ⁻) for absorption ∣F m_F⟩ → ∣F′ m_F + q_γ⟩; the operator index q_op = m_lower − m_upper = −q_γ | Steck QAO Eqs. 7.188-7.190, 7.419-7.422. Not: Steck's tables listing σ⁺ under q = −1; Berkeland's E_{+1}, E₀, E_{−1}, which are σ⁻, π, σ⁺ (relabelled at ingest) |
| 3j polarization index | read q off the column ordering of the equation implemented, never across equations: (J_f J_i 1; −m_f m_i q) forces q = m_f − m_i, (J_i 1 J_f; −m_i q m_f) forces q = m_i − m_f | Berkeland Eqs. 4, 12. Not: importing one into the other, which zeroes every σ channel and breaks trace preservation **[recomputed here]** |
